title: GM George Paton on building the Broncos’ roster: ‘It’s ongoing’
text: Hey, George, thanks for talking us to to us tonight. Uh, can you just talk about the decision to move on from or to wave Justin Jolie and how difficult that was as a uh fifth round pick this year and and what that says about the team. >> Sorry. >> I mean, you know, Justin, uh, you know, talented player, we knew it when we drafted him. Um, we knew he was raw. Um, and we still like the player. You know, he was coming on towards the end of training camp. You know, tight end position is a tough position for a rookie. He missed a lot of the off seasonason, just a little bit behind. You know, we wish we had another game or two. Um we we still like the player. We think he's going to have a nice career. You know, you just got to make tough decisions and and uh you know, and and to build the best 53 you can make. >> Eric Dala, Denver Broncos.com. >> George, you mentioned those tough decisions. You said uh earlier this offseason it was going to be a tough roster to make. Um just in your time here, was this the toughest roster to make? And um does that speak to the the strength of this team? >> Yeah, I think it does. I mean, every year is hard, you know, regardless of your depth. I mean, this is a tough day. Um um and it's always challenging with this year. I think we spent more time on this roster going through a lot of different scenarios. It's a lot of these players that were released and and uh it's a puzzle. It's ongoing. Uh we're now we're building the practice squad. We're looking at the wire tonight obviously and and so it's a fluid um it's fluid but yet yeah this was a tough roster to make you know and and for a draft picks obviously and and uh and so yeah it was more difficult. >> We'll try Parker Gabriel again. Go ahead Parker. >> Hey George. Sorry about that. Um obviously you've got experience behind Bo uh at quarterback with Jarrett and Sam. I'm curious just what went into the decision ultimately to keep three and along with that there was a lot of movement around the league today with you know number two and three quarterbacks. Did you feel any interest in those guys as you put this roster together? >> No, we love the quarterback room. I mean we stated that a lot. I mean Samy, we thought they both had really good offseasons, really good training camps and and uh and in the games. Um you know Sam's a big part of this quarterback room. We didn't want to lose him that we felt we were going to lose him. he's too important to our team. Um, and just didn't want to risk doing that. Obviously, the game you played the other night was outstanding. So, um, we love the room. We're going to keep the room together. >> Andrew Mason, the fan. >> Yeah, George, kind of what went into the decision on the back end at running back with Tyler Bedet over Jalom Mofflin there? >> Yeah, I mean, that was really tough. Um, really all three of those runners, you know, they're all really good runners. Um, they're all different. Um, you know, a lot goes into it obviously. Um, I mean, Jal, man, he's one of the, man, he's something else. Was really important to this team. Uh, the passion, everything he brings. Uh, they're just two different, they're two different, they got two different skill sets. Um, without going into too much detail. Um, so that was just, you detail, it was a really hard decision. Um, obviously special teams are involved. uh third down a bit. There's a lot involved, but um and that was probably the last decision we made is, you know, this fourth runner. >> Arie Stapleton, the Associated Press. >> Hey, George, a couple things I wanted to ask you about. Can you just speak to the decision by the commissioner to, you know, start off with Cooper on the um on the exemption list and then um secondly, what was your toughest cut do you think today? Yeah, I mean in regards to Jonathan, you know, being placed in the commissioner exempt uh you know, part of the process. Um, you know, we continue to take this very serious. We're going to monitor, you know, all the the legal developments and continue to support Jonathan. Um, Jonathan's worked very hard to better himself and and it'll be good to have him in in the building, be in meetings, and and uh just be a part of the team. Um, the toughest cut, I mean, they're all tough, man. There's not an easy cut. I just mentioned one. Um, and so I'll just stick with that, you know, with Jalil Mcloffslin, but there's others. I mean, this this, you know, as I was mentioned before, um, this was a hard one, you know, we were up late. We've been we've been at it, you know, since after the first preseason game, we knew this was coming. Um, but they're all hard and and you know, I just talked about Julio. That was especially tough for what he's meant to this team and and uh what he's meant to this organization. >> Chris Thomas in the Gazette. >> Yeah. Hey, George. Uh you currently don't have a long snapper. Uh what was the thinking on releasing Mitchell? Is he a vested guy that's going to go to the practice squad? And I know that you also let Luke Basso go. >> Yeah, Mitch Mitch is going to be on our, you know, our practice squad. He'll be a practice squad veteran. You know, they don't have to to clear waiverss. Um you know, just provides, you know, flexibility, you know, within the roster, uh throughout the season, you know, when they start here. And so that's all it was. >> Mike Cliff, 9 News. >> Yes, George. I was just going to say uh you figured out how to basically have a 55man roster with what you're doing with Mitch Raboni and and Apprentice. Could you could you speak to that little gymnastic and and also the roster construction on defense where uh you keep seven defensive linemen which is maybe a little heavy and then because of the Cooper only four outside linebackers and and the four inside. Yeah, I mean, you know, with the Dline, Mike, you know, Dline and O line, the priority we we put in those positions and and the depth that those positions have really helped us the last couple years and and and a large part of our um success. And so, you know, um Jordan, you know, he he's, you know, we got some youth in front of him. Um he's been a good player the last couple years and we just didn't want to lose him. Um and in regards to, you know, uh Fab Brone, you know, I just talked about it, Mike. It just gives us flexibility. Um, you know, the expanded practice squad allows that. Um, obviously, you know, you have other, you know, you can elevate. There's certain things you can do with your roster and and it's just part of it, the roster management. >> Jeff Glald, ESPN. >> Do you have any concerns uh any of the the draft picks in particular, Jolie and Murdoch, uh, are are risk for waiver claims? Yeah, I mean we we're you always worry, you know, um about the guys you want to bring back, you know, that they could get claimed and and uh and if we do, like we told them, we're going to give them a hug and wish them the best. That's part of it. That's part of the league. Um obviously, it's a risk when you put guys like out out there. Um but again, it's just part of it. And uh you know, we're going to be looking a lot of other rosters, you know, uh tonight as well. I think there'll be 1100 guys on the roster, but you know, last year I think there was only 26 guys claimed and so um you know, we'll just kind of see maybe the number is going to be greater this year, but we we've kind of weighed that Jeff. Um but yeah, you it's always a risk. >> Troy rank the Denver Post. >> George, what is your trust level with Jonah Ellis and DeAndre Tilman and Q Robinson behind Cooper and certainly not really knowing how long he's going to be gone? Were you comfortable with the number of reps they were able to get in camp? >> Yeah, and these guys have all played in games, big games, and done well, you know. Um, all these guys would feel like we can play. We like the depth there. Um, I mean, we led the league in sacks the last two years. These guys were all a part of that. Q coming on late. I think you saw what Q did uh you know the the New England game you know late in the season even Houston game last year some of the things he did and then you watched him in training camp and the games this year u we feel really good about him and then Jonah and and and obviously Tilly and Nick I mean these guys have played and they've done well um yeah depth wise you know we'll be looking a little bit um looking on the practice squad we'll be looking around um you can never have enough pass rushers so um you know we'll just kind of see how that goes. Hy Frederickson the Gazette. >> Hey George with Caleb Loner going on IR. I'm just curious if you could give us an update on just how his injury recovery is going and also just how you project him um in this offense offense just with sort of a limited amount of time getting to evaluate him. >> Yeah, I mean he he's looked good. You know, he was having a really good off seasonason. Obviously had a setback uh with the foot. You know, we expect him I'm not sure the timet mid-season maybe. Don't hold me to that. Um, but he has he has all the traits. Uh, obviously size, he can run. He's got great ball skills being a basketball uh player. He just, you know, this this would have been a really important preseason training camp for him. He just needs reps. We're still excited about him. He's here every day working. Um, but obviously uh we won't we won't see him until uh you know, late October or so. >> We have time for two more questions. We'll go Darren McKe and then Brandon Crystalall. Go ahead Darren. >> Hey George. Um, do you have any specific examples of something that happened in the last preseason game that impacted any decisions made today? >> Um, that's a great question. Um, you know, typically you look at the body of work. This this is kind of the cherry on top. That last preseason game, we had a number of guys play well. You know, whether it's Jordan, Jack, you know, I don't think it impacted a lot of these guys. You know, I think um as it would in a lot of years, you know what I mean? I think we were pretty set on what on where we were. I think we were probably at uh you know 55 54 before the last game and maybe it just tweaked a little. I I don't really have a great example for you. I mean Sam obviously played played great. If we were thinking anything there that certainly confirmed keeping Sam but um I don't have a great answer but good question. >> Final question. Brandon Crystalall Gorilla Sports. Hey George, you know Sean's talked about it and I asked him again Friday about he hates losing a guy that then goes and has success. And so you mentioned that only 26 guys were claimed, but are have you been preparing for the idea that your roster's been good, y'all drafted well or brought guys in that you're going to lose guys you really do want back and they are going to go have success somewhere else? >> I think that's part of it. I mean, I think um I told a number of these guys, you know, and I I think I just mentioned it. If if they get if they get claimed, we're going to shake their hand. We're going to give them a hug. We're going to root for them. We root for these guys. No different than losing a scout, losing assistant GM. You know, man, you're rooting for them. You want these guys to do well. Um these guys have put in a lot of work, um dedication. Uh we love these players. We want them to do well. We hope they're here obviously, but if not here, we wish them the best and and you never know what happens here down the road. Um we like this group. We like this this this group that's going to be on the waiverss tonight. Um we'd love to get a lot of them back and we'll just see how it goes. But yeah, to answer your question, we just wish him well. >> George, thank you so much for taking the time today.

title: Jesse Minter: ‘Joe Fagnano Legitimately Played His Way Onto the Roster’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: you guys being here. First one of really just congratulate um you know, making a 53-man roster is a major deal. Try to really sell that to the guys like not to take it for granted. Obviously, everybody's in a different position. You got guys that have played for a long time, but you got, you know, undrafted free agents making the team. It's a really cool scenario when you kind of see it all all come together. So, major shout-out to those guys. Also, major you know, congrats and shout-out to all the guys we added on the practice squad. It's a it's a huge deal, especially with the rules now. You know, I kind of look at it as a a 70-man roster um with with the numbers that we have that they're all ready to play that we that we need to have all every single guy as part of that 70 ready to play at the drop of a hat when their number's called. Uh that's what we really want those guys to focus on. Um we'll we'll kind of uh we'll operate today with the practice. Tomorrow, we won't practice. Uh we'll we'll spend the day celebrating Justin Tucker and everything that he's meant to the Ravens organization. Uh we'll practice again on Wednesday and Thursday. The guys will be out of here on Thursday for the four-day break. Uh we'll be back on Tuesday ready to roll headed into Indy. So, that's kind of our plan for the week and uh open it up for questions. >> Jesse, uh you added Jake Moody to the practice squad. Uh a lot of available kickers out there to bring to the What what was the decision process? >> Yeah, Jake's just kind of been on the radar um and he's a guy that's had success in this league and you know, really just felt like add a guy and and um you know, it's whatever's best for the team at that particular moment. So, uh we added a guy to to compete on the practice squad and uh kind of see how it shakes out from there. >> What would you kind of like to see out of the competition like that? >> I mean, I I don't really I I have a lot of confidence in Tyler still. Uh I think again, he's had a great training camp. I expect him to be our kicker going into Indianapolis. Uh but I think again, you're always trying to just have every scenario covered. Um And so that's what we're trying to do as a team. >> Jesse, what can you uh say about the decision to keep three quarterbacks and not go with two? >> You know, I go back to the other day where it's like, you know, the last spot or two often comes down to the best player. And the player that who's the best player? Really the kind of the player that plays the best. Um, and so I just give Joe like a ton of credit for how he played. He he legitimately played his way onto this roster. And just felt like it gave us the best situation uh for the quarterbacks. Um, again, a guy that that probably we probably would have had a lot of interest from other teams with the way that he played. And so uh you don't want to let good players like that leave your building. And so uh very happy for Joe, proud of Joe, proud of the way that he played. I thought Izzy did a great job with him throughout training camp. Um, and so we're happy to have him. >> Jesse, you probably had quite a lot of difficult conversations and had to let go. What are the conversations like with a guy like Joe who almost made the team? >> Yeah, it's really cool. Um, you know, and I heard him speak after the game and it was like, you know, he could go to he could go sleep easy that night knowing that he kind of did everything in his power, everything in his control. This is a guy that took advantage of every rep. Um, and then when his number was called and the lights were on like really performed. So when you get to have those conversations, it's really really cool. Um, again, a guy that just earned his way. And and that's really uh kind of kind of hoped that that would be the case at the start of camp that there would be guys that just, you know, and Ethan Burke as well. Like these guys just played their way onto the roster, didn't worry about the numbers. And people saying, "Well, they'll only keep this amount of this position." Or this guy was whatever. Those guys didn't worry about any of that and played their way onto the roster. And it's major credit to them. >> Jesse, what happened to the pass rusher race wise? What was it that he did that was maybe the tipping point that he was the one who made it? >> You know, I think he's just been really consistent. And when you look at when you look at uh particularly two phases of the game that he's played really well on special teams and he's been really consistent on defense with what he can bring to the table really physical really rugged but it really good rusher he's had some really really good days rushing the passer out here in training camp and also in the preseason games I thought he's been dominant at times in special teams on the kickoff team in particular and so again just a guy that kind of played his way played his way into the team. >> What happened with Randall obviously he played he played well in the game and did he have something that you didn't realize he had during the game or what what kind of popped up? >> He's kind of been dealing with something and so you know we were able to get him back for that but he's dealing with something enough that we feel like this is the best situation for him to to get really healthy. I think he's got a bright future for us. I think he you know he's in a position to be able to come back and help us but it just gives him the opportunity to get fully healthy. That's what he's dealing with. >> The decision to not have Nnamdi start on IR just kind of what went into that and what are you expecting to see from him over the next couple weeks as you kind of get into the preseason? >> Yeah again um similar to I think the the path that's been all along he's progressing more and more and more and more and so he's you know we'll kind of evaluate these next couple weeks and and but I I don't anticipate it being something where he's not you know when you when you do that you're talking about four games if you if you were to start him there so um you know I don't see him obviously missing that many games. >> Will he do any full team work this week? >> Yeah he's the he's just doing more and more and it kind of leave it to the plan leave it to what we're doing but he's he's in a really good position. >> Just go just go back to to Joe real quick. Were you you know especially given the circumstances were you surprised that he seemed to kind of handle it as well as he did and played as well as he did? >> You know like I think surprised is like a a funny way because that just means like maybe you didn't think that he had it in him Um, and so not to not to say that, but like very impressed because, um, you know, at this at the start we didn't even sign him right after the draft. If we added him a few days later, we added a couple rookies. I thought I thought early on, you know, he sort of, um, was the better of the two rookies and then, you know, but we added a veteran, so then his reps went down even more. And so, I would say just really impressed by like that week of the Philly game, he started to get a few more reps and, um, looked pretty poised and comfortable for not for not having had a lot. And then I think in the games it just really took off for him and his confidence really really took off and grew. To me, when you play like that, like you're already a pretty confident guy to be able to kind of handle, uh, not having the reps that he had and be able to go in and operate. So, again, it's really just a credit to him and kind of the the uh, player that he is, the cool demeanor that he carries. Uh, doesn't really get rattled and obviously with a quarterback, that's a great quality. I think we're still evaluating that. Uh, we'll we'll probably have, uh, you know, over the next week or so kind of figure that out, but I still think that that's a that's a real, uh, competition. >> All right, thanks, coach. >> Thank you.

title: Is the Ravens' Front Seven Too Old?
text: Smith, great to have you with us. Same thing with John Morris. And Jack, Jack wants more. He says it's the Ravens front seven too old, which goes back to kind of the beginning part of our conversation there, Jeff, with why the Aeneas Peebles conversation in particular is an interesting one. >> Yeah. >> And let's start talking defensive line. Great segue from Jack. >> Yeah, I think you look at it and assuming Calais Campbell's on this roster, it's going to be Calais Campbell, Calais Campbell, Travis Jones, John Jenkins, um Broderick Washington. That's five, right? >> And then the sixth will be Aeneas Peebles. And even six feels maybe one too many if you're paying attention to what Justin Minter did last year. You know, are they too old? I don't know. I mean, Calais Campbell's not old. Travis Jones is not old. I think you look at John Jenkins, you're fine as long as you're not overplaying him. He's a backup nose tackle who shouldn't be playing much more than a dozen snaps a game. 10, 12 snaps. He's not too old for that, but I think you're always looking for young blood. And and you know, you'd like to be a little younger there for sure. Will be a fatal flaw of this team? I don't know. I mean, I guess it depends if the injuries hit. It's something to watch, but think that's why they don't want to play Calais Campbell a ton of snaps. They've talked about this. And it's all about Calais Campbell, man. Even some of the roster decisions. If he's not ready to go early this season, you need to take six cuz you're basically committing to having only five the rest of the season. You can't go five with Calais Campbell and then know he may not be available the first couple weeks. Cuz then you're going to every game with four defensive linemen. And one of those guys is What is Is Jenkins 34 or is he even older than that? >> He's damn near right around there. >> Yeah. And then Calais Campbell, who we've discussed. So, it's it's um it's different, you know, it's different. That's why I'm I'm going six Matt Ioannidis on the team cuz I think even if he's not there week one or two, if you get him back for week three, it's worth it. If it That's what it takes. Um but he's kind of the elephant in the room. We still haven't We have not talked to Ndamukong Suh since like week one last year and um so it's so hard to get a key get a any gauge on what's going on there. I just did not like Jesse's response. Not from a negative. I did I just it didn't He's really optimistic sometimes about some of the injuries and guys making great progress and there wasn't that optimistic tone like, "Look, we think he's got a good shot." You know, it's kind of like, "Yeah, we don't have an answer to that." So. >> Could not definitively give an answer. >> Yeah. So. >> turns 38 in July. Unbelievable. Next year. >> Yeah. Yeah. And look, Akiem Hicks is a guy I'd probably like to keep around, right? Like young nose tackle. I think he got better a little bit last year. >> Massive dude. >> Yeah, but you How many nose tackles you going to keep? So, I mean maybe like there sometimes there's a surprise cut. Like is Jenkins on the hot seat? I I don't have any info I don't have any information to suggest he is. Like he's perfect for that role as a reserve nose tackle run stuffer and he's a great guy at team guy who people love in the locker room. He's been great for Travis Jones. So, you'd think they'd keep him around, but you know, if you want to get younger, you have Benny or T.J. Cleam make the team and John Jenkins not make it. That's one way to get a little younger there. >> But as of right now, you got guys like Akiem Hicks practice squad candidate outside looking in. You got O'Ajeiga outside looking in. >> Who I like. I think O'Ajeiga has played really well this and he you know you could get him to be the extra practice squad guy. Gives you an extra guy cuz he's got the international designation. >> We're fired up about a brand new partnership and it is with our friends at SeatGeek. Click the link that we have in the description, download the app, have the code automatically added to your account so you can use it for later. >> So guys like him, guys like Rayshawn Berry. >> I certainly would like to keep Berry around. You know, I think he's he could develop into do a rotational guy. So yeah, but that's I'm going six. >> But would I be shocked if if at 4:00 Sunday they sent out the roster only as five? No, I wouldn't be. I think that's one area where Minter has shown he's not afraid to go short. I think you're also going to see Tavis Robinson, Zaire Young play inside. So, they probably won't look five as being all that short when you're going to move those guys inside in different packages. >> Sure. Okay. Well, let's go outside now then. Trey Hendrickson, Mike Green, Tavis Robinson, Zion Young is four and four absolute locks. And then after that, it gets interesting. >> Yeah, I think the biggest story at that position coming into camp in terms of roster was will they keep a fifth to keep as uh Adisa Isaac around. Now, I think that's evolved to will they keep a fifth and will that fifth be Ethan Burke, Adisa Isaac, or K'Waun Rocker. I I'm thinking Rocker is the third guy. So, I'm not you know, but I I like that kid. I think he's played really well and and he played well last week, but it just there's no room at the inn as they like to say. So, I I I think they keep five. I just think that's a critical position. You want to keep the extra guy, but what do you do there? Like, do you just say, "Look, we've seen enough of Adisa Isaac. It's just it's never going to happen. He's just never going to get developed. Uh let's give this other young kid who's outplayed Adisa Isaac this summer." I don't think Adisa Isaac's been bad at all. I think he's been noticeable. And again, Adisa Isaac has NFL special teams reps. That's the other thing. That fifth linebacker spot, that's going to come in handy. I think you'll both see them on front line special teams units tomorrow. It's always That's always, you know, I don't When you're watching the final preseason game, look at who's on the front line special teams. If you're deciding on roster decisions, that's usually a way where you get I always tell the story how Zach Gore, uh undrafted rookie linebacker from, you know, North Texas, who we were giving no chance to make the team, all of a sudden we're looking out there in the second preseason game and he's on the first team special teams. It's like, "Wait wait a second." Well, yeah, he made the roster, too. That usually is a kind of a giveaway. It At least it was in the Harbaugh era. We We may be a little different here, but um to me, I think that's a position where you got to keep five. You have three young guys. Um why not see if one of them can develop, even if he's a game day scratch most days? You get him developing. What I would do, I would probably go with Burke cuz I think he's best, but he just can't dis- You can't dismiss the Ravens wanting to get more out of that third-round pick they spent on Adebayo Isaac and feeling like he has more to give if he can just stay healthy. Let's be willing to give him another shot to stay healthy to see if he can do it and to see if he improves and we can start reaping some of the rewards from the pick we spent. I would go Burke, but I would not be at all surprised if they go Isaac for that fifth spot, but I I think it's probably between those two guys and I would list those two guys on a very short list. I'd probably say there's four or five defensive players on a short list competing for maybe two spots Friday night. That's what I see. I think there's probably not much more than two or three spots still left in their mind and I think there's four or five guys defensively competing for them. >> Just when you think all the rah-rahs on the back end with the >> Yeah, totally. >> Not so fast. Nuno writes uh if Nnadi's only available for week five or six, do you see him as an IR option? So >> I mean, you you have to. You have to. Like, that's that's late. I mean, five or six is not even close to make cuz Yeah, we're 2 weeks away from even starting the season. So, you're talking 8 weeks down the road. Yeah, I think you have to. But again, it it has to be considered when you're on IR, you can't practice with the team. And what this guy needs is live reps in practice, and he can't get them. So, um that's where I say, "Look, if he's 2 weeks behind, and you can get him back for week three, I think it's worth it to keep him. But you start talking to you you're projecting him late September, October, you almost have to you know, put him on IR. Cuz if he's on your team, and he can't play for those first four, five weeks, you're playing short on defensive line, or you're keeping an extra defensive lineman, which hurts you at another roster spot. >> Appreciate you, Nuno. And before we continue on with the defense, Colin, just kind of revisiting something we discussed earlier on in the show. He says, "Is Broddy Washington a cut candidate? Who are players to watch tomorrow? The tight end group seems like it will be solid this year."

I saw him today. If he isn't unbelievable in terms of getting mental reps cuz he didn't get a ton of of the physical reps. So, it says a lot about him cuz there still is a small sample size right to go by, but what you look at and you say, well, he did that with the limited amount of reps that he got. He did a great job of embracing Um it's not a sexy spot you know, to go from one to catch a lot of passes and envisioning scoring touchdowns to kicking out an end on power. It's really not, you know, what he's dreaming of but I thought he embraced that part of it and you can see his confidence growing in the physical part of it. I think that's probably when you're moving somebody from an on-the-line player and route runner to in the backfield it it takes time and you don't get that in the spring. You never have pads on, right? Until we actually put the pads on, you really don't see certain elements of the tight ends, fullbacks, O-line. You just You just don't. And you don't see it with receivers and skill players who you can trust little guys blocking little guys. >> How to help You mentioned this on Thursday a little bit with Taylen's play in the end zone where he got the 30-yard run in the preseason. It's not quite the same all that. I've said that all, you know, 20 years ago Shedeur would have been considered a dual threat. And it's just changed over 20 years. Now, the athleticism has grown. It starts at the high school level. Who these teams have playing quarterback cuz they're going to put it in their hands, going to put the best athlete the best player there and then develop develop their throwing skills. That's It's easier that way than it is to think you're going to be a throwing team. Almost at every level. So, >> [clears throat] >> I do think that you're seeing more and more athleticism at the position. I do think that there is that balance between the loss shortage plays and play-making ability. Somewhere in there as a player gets better and better, uh they learn the idea of when to eliminate a catastrophic play and still use their athleticism. Uh that was one of those in the end zone the other night like, "Oh, all right." Um came out the other side feeling pretty good, but wouldn't have had We would have had a safety there. Uh but again, when you have players like that, they're going to have to work through that. That's They're going to want to make a play and and you're going to have to live with some of the other stuff. >> Pretty good? >> Pretty good. All right. Thank you.

What have you seen about his personal process that has helped him translate even in training camp when he's not getting all those necessarily physical reps? >> Well, he's he's very diligent. He's a diligent noteaker. You look at his notes. So is so is Dylan. But you know, Tailon, he stands back there even in the walks. I can see him mentally going through the reps. So I think that's the biggest thing looking at film mentally going through the reps. Not maybe getting the physical rep, but he gets the mental part of it. And then, you know, some of his just um his athleticism that ends up taking over. Todd, I know I think you have 10 rookies, made the initial 53, and some will have bigger roles than others, but how do you tell if a guy who's never played in the league is ready for week one? Like, what are you looking for specific things? >> Well, you can only go by what you've seen. You can only go by initially practice, how they've performed, and then how they performed in the preseason games. That's the closest you're going to get. So, you don't know for sure, but I feel pretty good about situations we put them in in practice and then in the preseason games that they'll be able to play at a at an extremely high level, but you don't know till you go and play. And then, you know, all of those players have talent, so they're only going to continue to get better. We're going to continue to roll them out there and and uh we're going to continue to improve. >> Along those lines with Michael Coach Jr. and him making the initial 53. What did you guys see from him and and like about him throughout this training camp just being the only undrafted rookie to make? >> Well, there's a lot to like just how he goes about his daily preparation. Um, and he made a bunch of plays. I mean, let's just say it like it is. I mean, every day he walked out there, he made a bunch of plays. So, it's it's real easy. I mean, that's that's what you should do. You should reward the players that make a bunch of plays in camp. And that's that's what he did. We we in the media voted most outstanding rookie in camp. It's a prestigious award. [laughter] Did he did he come along even faster than you expected? >> I don't know if faster is is the uh is the word but uh we are pleased with his progress. I think we hoped and anticipated that he would bring, you know, the things that we had seen on tape from return value to uh just getting the ball in his hands and then his route running down the field. Uh we had seen contested catches and I think uh from a ball skill standpoint, he's been great. >> In your coaching career, have you seen a player like coach who didn't play high school ball walked on junior college, worked his way up and then made NFL roster like that? Uh, I'd have to look at that, but I'm sure there's somewhere in there, I've been around somebody that, you know, started off playing a different sport and then ended up making an NFL roster. Um, I was never with him, but I was at Eastern Michigan with Antonio Gates. He showed up there for like a semester playing noon hoops with us. And, uh, then he left. I don't know, Michigan State, US, Kent. I think he end up somewhere in there. obviously had a heck of a career. So, that's the only one I can really think of where it's translate. Now, we're talking about an elite player, but obviously I think Michael's age helps that, you know, I think uh but it's it's been fun to watch. >> Todd, was it always your guys playing quarterbacks even before you found out? >> I won't get into that. I mean, we obviously liked all of our quarterbacks and we certainly didn't want to lose any of them. 10 10 offensive line are lot. Why do you feel the need to keep 10? >> Well, really it I thought Zack Zenner played his way onto the roster the way he played the last two games. You know, he got he got dinged up a little bit early in camp and I thought he played his way on the roster. >> One more on KC, please. When even when he was drafted, he had that reputation of drops. He talked about how he wanted to work on that. How has he improved that and what did he do to get better? >> Well, the way we saw it um coming out of college, we thought they were a little bit more concentration drops than lack of, you know, ball skill traits that we thought he had and he's just done a better job of that. He's worked hard getting on the jugs and working with the coaches. So, again, and he's made a number of contested catches and catches outside of his framework. So, again, it's been impressive. Todd, you know about [clears throat] the uh Pride, the young man you you claimed off waiverss from from Buffalo, and what what are you you looking at him potentially coming in and where helping out at? >> Well, we practiced against him and uh really like the way he played and covered and competed and we're always trying to upgrade the roster. He just kind of happened to to fit that as we'd looked at after we got done practicing with them. uh his name came up. Uh should he be, you know, 53 casualty? Would be would we have interest? And the answer was yes. >> I was talking to Spencer last week about his footwork and how he developed it throughout the draft process and even since he's been here. What has stood out to you about the way he se? Well, he always had that the athleticism piece of it, but I think where he's really evolved is uh his upper body with his lower body in terms of his movement and his punch and not getting overextended and and Jared going against him every day has helped that. But I think just the coordination of it all and I think it's only going to continue to get better. >> I'm just wondering since you made the exceiver and decided to move around. >> What has Judy's attitude been? >> Been great. In fact, I met with him today and he was great. You know, we just feel like that we want the ability to keep him on the move and whether it's at Z or F. And I think we could still play him at X, we want to be able to move him around and we wanted to see how Denzel would uh would function as our ex receiver. And >> wouldn't an ex receiver consider that an emotion? >> Um, I don't see it that way. I mean I I mean he didn't see it that way as far as I understand. I mean it was really in his mind I think he believes he is better on the move and you know I think I think he could see like hey what could we what we could do with him and move him around and keep him on the move and motion when when you're ex I mean you're for the most part you're stationary. We don't have a chance to motion and shift you and and get your speed and your ability to separate. >> So you don't view X receiver as a number one receiver per se? I don't I I don't view it as that. I just view it as we're trying to put the pieces where we can uh best allow us to function offensively. So, I really don't care who plays X or who plays Z um other than what we're going to ask them to do per se uh within a given game plan. And obviously there's any 3x one set your ex is going to be isolated. And so we just thought that Denzel's skill set gave us some things there that Jerry didn't. And we thought Jerry's skill set uh playing off of the ball uh allowed us to really maximize his skill set. >> Will we see Bond out there today or is he still >> I don't know. I saw him today uh as far as I know he's been clear, but I think it's still deter to be determined whether we'll see him today. Within obviously it's one thing to take a flyer on a guy in the sixth round to keep him on the roster in a crowded quarterback room. What does that say about, you know, what you guys can see for for his future down the road? >> Well, I mean, that doesn't happen if he isn't diligent, if he isn't unbelievable in terms of getting mental reps because he didn't get a ton of of the physical reps. So, it says a lot about him because there still is a small sample size, right, to go by, but what you look at and you say, well, he did that with the limited amount of reps that he got. Let's we certainly want to see more. It's hard to get that. It just is. But we we were impressed uh with his ability to handle information, operate on the field, and then and then make the plays that he made. What do you see as his potential if he can Mary obviously his obvious physical gifts with some of the stuff that he still needs to catch up on? >> Well, it remains to be seen. I mean, we like the start. I think that's the best way to put it with a lot of young players. We like the start that he's had. Now, where we go from here, there's I mean, we don't know what the future holds in terms of uh our health of the quarterback room and where we go, but we like the start he's had. >> Was it always the plan to have a fullback? I mean, I know you want Michael for that reason, but you always figured he was gonna be on the 53. >> Yes. >> Just because you figure you think it's that important in whatever settings you do. >> Well, you're gonna I mean, whether it's short yardage, whether it's goal line, whether it's coming out fourminute, I mean, I think you're going to want a fullback. You're going to want the ability to play downhill. And he Mike gives us that. [music] I mean, all you had to see when he came back a week ago and the reps he took, you could see a guy that had played fullback and really understands the position. There's guys that played fullback and there's guys that have played fullback and play at it played at elite level and Mike's the latter. >> Now that we're at this point, if you look back at it, could you estimate how many major decisions were made as a result of the joint practice? >> How many major decisions? the ultimate decision making. >> There was probably a big part of that. I would probably say that that the joint practices were as big as anything. I wouldn't go so far as to say whatever percentage was on it. But I do think it was big. I do think it was the one opportunity that we had. Again, we only moved the ball one block and we only had one two minutes. So, we really weren't stacking plays, but it was somewhat of our best on their best, and that gave you probably the best indication of what you can expect. I mean, all we can go by is what we've seen in the past, the greater predict, the greatest prediction of the future is the past. And so, that's what we went by uh in making a number of the decisions. >> You talked about a couple more. You talk about the fullback and Michael Burton's role. I know you would sort of tried out Brian Carson Ryan and some of that as well. How How far along did he kind of come and living up to what you had kind of envisioned fullback? >> Well, Carson really came a long ways. I mean, it's um it's one thing for us to have a vision of it and then what he'd really done in college and then embracing that, which he did. He did a great job of embracing that. Um, it's not a sexy spot, you know, to go from wanting to catch a lot of passes and envisioning scoring touchdowns to kicking out an end on power. It's really not, you know, what he's dreaming of, but I thought he embraced that part of it. And you can see his confidence growing in the physical part of it. I think that's probably when you're moving somebody from an on the-line player and route runner to in the back field. It it takes time and you don't get that in the spring. We never have pads on, right? Until we actually put the pads on, you really don't see certain elements of the tight ends, fullbacks, O line. You just you just don't. And you don't see it with receivers and skilled players who you can trust, little guys blocking little guys. Todd, you mentioned this on Thursday a little bit with Taylor's play in the end zone where he got the 30 yard run. It was preseason and it's not quite the same all that, but with more quarterbacks coming in with exceptional mobility skill sets, how have coaches evolved their thinking on you got to get rid of the ball versus, you know, let them let them play make a little bit? >> Well, I don't know if they've changed their mindset in it, but um it has definitely changed. I've said that all, you know, 20 years ago, Shadur would have been considered a dual threat and it's just changed over 20 years. Now [music] the athleticism has grown. It starts at the high school level who these teams have playing quarterback because they're going to put it in their hands. You're going to put the best athlete, the best player there, and then develop develop their throwing skills. That's it's easier that way than it is to think you're going to be a throwing team almost at every level. So, [clears throat] I do think that you're seeing more and more athleticism at the position. I do think that there is that balance between the lost yardage plays and playmaking ability somewhere in there as a player gets better and better. Uh, they learn the idea of when to eliminate a catastrophic play and still use their athleticism. Uh that was one of those in the end zone the other night like oh all right. Um came out the other side feeling pretty good but wouldn't have had a safety there. Uh but again when you have players like that they're going to have to work through that. That's they're going to want to make a play and and you're going to have to live with some of the other stuff. >> Pretty good. >> All right. Thank you. Sorry, Ashley. >> Hello.

title: LIVE REACTION: Buffalo Bills Set 53-Man Roster | Always Gameday in Buffalo
text: Hey Bills Mafia, we know there's one thing on your mind everyday. Your team, the Buffalo Bills. So, Matt Bove and Sal Capaccio are here to bring you the latest news, notes, and opinions straight from the source, right here, right now. Because it's always game day in Buffalo. >> [music] >> Well, it's finally done. The Bills 53-man initial roster is set. Anything can change over the next, you know, day, but even beyond, of course. It's always game day in Buffalo. Live reaction to it. Welcome in. Matt Bove is right there. I'm Sal Capaccio. Matt, I would say before we get into the nitty-gritty of the numbers and the names, would you agree that this is most maybe the more the most surprising 53-man roster that we've had in several years? >> Yes and no. I don't know if anything is big enough to truly be a surprise, but there were a lot of little surprises, if that makes sense. >> mean, you might have one or two recently, but there felt like there were more than that this year. >> Yeah, I thought going into today, as I started to see the cuts today trickle in on Sunday morning, you know, some of our colleagues were reporting different cuts that were happening. I felt really good about the 53-man roster I had put together, and I was like, oh, I might be like 100% here, or I might be really, really close to it. And then, as we got closer to 6:00, and we saw a couple of the other moves happen, Can Walker was the first kind of big domino to fall, about like, whoa, that's a little weird. And then, I think that will lead us to a lot of the conversation we have this evening. But, yeah, like Mike Dana was a surprise. Ko Kiefer Lotu was a surprise. Dwayne Carter making the team, Jude Bowery making the team outright, not going to IR. Zane Durant going to IR. So, there was like a lot of little things that threw me off. What did you think? >> First of all, I I think that your wherever you're sitting is awesome in the background. I just want to tell you that if people are watching it. Like, where are you now? You're Sometimes you're just like in your office with your the stuff like I have. >> Yeah. >> Is that like Where is that? Your living room? What is that? >> No, it's just my basement now. Yeah, my basement because we needed to do some renovating in our house. This desk used to be over there. >> No, I Yeah, thank you. I appreciate that. I've got, you know, over my one shoulder that's that hole-in-one plaque. What do you know about hole-in-one, Sal? I don't know if you do. Under it, that's a picture of my dad and I at Oak Hill from back in 2003. I love that photo. Actually, in the bottom, you see that like thing over right under that photo that's like a buffalo cutout? Yes. That was from my wedding and everybody at my wedding signed it like with a message to my wife and I. So, that's like a cool thing to have. Yeah, so I got some cool Thanks for the shout-out. Yeah. >> Yeah, I mean, that looks really nice. All right, thanks for the shout-out to Cold Blooded Candace. How about that for a name? She is catching us from Albuquerque. Thank you very much, Cold Blooded Candace. >> Candace? >> Finally finally a chance to see us live. Keep the um keep the comments rolling. We'll kind of run through some of them. Somebody says you're wearing Dolphins colors. I don't know. I don't think so. He's just got a a cap that might have that. Okay. You asked me my surprise, I think, like Yeah, I was I was surprised about Kenai Walker. Now, someone in the chat said, "Why should we be surprised?" I'll go back to do this here. Let's go to this comment here. I don't get why people are so shocked about an undrafted rookie who was never going to be CB4. We need experience in that position. I don't know. Do you need experience in that position? That might be a position where you can actually bring a younger guy along. The Bills have done that in the past. They've had, you know, I know they weren't in the necessarily the same position they are now, but they've had Levi Wallace and Dane Jackson. They have outside corners that were I mean, heck, they started a rookie last year at outside corner, and Max Harrison. >> I don't even know how much of the surprise is specifically tied to Kenai Walker. The biggest surprise to me is that they only kept three boundary corners, two boundary corners on their roster. That's very light. Now, there are layers to this and we'll talk about this more. D'Shawn Alford, their starting nickel cornerback, has position flexibility. So, in a pinch, he could play outside and because they love Jordan Hancock, the primary backup to D'Shawn Alford, they don't think they'd probably be losing a ton if they had to have D'Shawn Alford at the boundary and then Jordan Hancock at nickel. Here's the problem though, you're one injury away from a real big problem and if that injury is Christian Benford, it's bigger than a real big problem. I think they need to go out. I actually think adding a veteran corner might be more significant than going and adding a returner cuz I think those are the two things now for the next 48 hours that we probably need to pay attention to cuz I can see a world where they go and do either of those things. >> Okay, but but your point is right about the injury, but there's a difference between having an injury in a game or having an injury that you have to, you know, put somebody in for the next couple weeks because that's what a practice squad is for. Whether you keep Kenai Walker or Toriano Pride on the active roster or not doesn't matter. If they're still in your building and you have an injury in the, you know, second quarter of a game, you try to get through that game and then you just pull them up from the practice squad the next week. I don't see it as much of a big deal for, you know, these guys are still on your team. You still have 17 practice squad players. But I agree with you going into a game with only three outside corners can be problematic unless, as you say, they really believe that a guy like D'Shawn Alford can do that and then Jordan Hancock can slide in. So, I think that was the initial surprise from a lot of people that they didn't keep a fourth boundary corner. Whether that's Kenai Walker or somebody else. So, let's let's call it right now. Do you think that they are actively looking to add to that spot to the 53 or would they just kind of play it by ear each week with those guys that we assume will be back on the practice squad. >> Yeah, it's tricky because once again, we're assuming that they get to the practice squad and Kanai Walker would be the most likely guy who might draw some attention from other teams. >> get snapped up. That's right. He could get and that's the risk that they have to be willing to take. >> I I don't know because I have questions besides Christian Benford. I have questions about the other two. That's why I would if I was them, like I would be prioritizing bringing in a veteran and you know, everybody assumes it's Tre' White. Like you look at the comments right now and I know what I'm talking about. >> up. Let me bring up the defense. Here we go. So people can take a look at exactly what we're talking about in the bottom half there. If you're If you're listening, we're looking at the Bills 53-man roster. If you're watching, those that are shaded and if you want to call it peach or a different color, rose, whatever. Yeah, those Yeah, they salmon, those players were released and then the ones in in white are on the team. Go ahead. >> So like that's what I'm saying with the let's look at outside cornerback. Christian Benford, I don't have any questions there. Max Carriston has only, you know, been healthy for what? Seven games or something? I don't even know what it is, but he was banged up multiple times his rookie year and this summer. And Igwebuike is an unproven player who doesn't have any NFL experience yet. So that's why I think if you can go out and find somebody and you know, all of these comments are about Tre' because Tre' is a guy who I've talked about pretty extensively going back to before training camp even started. I don't think it has to be Tre' White. I think that might be the easiest or quickest phone call to make or the easiest thing to piece together, but I don't love rolling the dice because let's say Kanai Walker go somewhere else, which I don't think is out of the realm of possibility. I don't I don't want to speak for you. I never after like a week or two was like, "Oh, Toriano Pride is going to make this team." I never had that feeling. So if he's the next man up, if we didn't even think he had a chance to make the 53-man roster, what makes you feel good about having to have him active on a game day? >> Let's keep it on the defensive side. The other big surprise for me on this side of the ball, and we debated the names, we didn't realize Zane Durant would go on IR. That kind of solves an issue for you. We knew Fedor Mathis would go on a suspended list, but they kept 12 overall defensive linemen. That counts interior defensive line with six and edge rushers another six. So, the numbers there to me seemed a little bit fat. I thought maybe they'd go with 11 overall maybe you have five at one and six at the other, but they do go with six and that includes Dwayne Carter and Greg Gaines, the two guys we talked about on the pod when we were at signals. And of course, Mike Dana as an edge rusher outside linebacker who clearly did enough in the preseason as a veteran to be on this team. He was the one that might have been the most, you know, on the cutline I guess for a lot of us and we didn't have him on the team. >> Yeah, so Zane Durant, he was going to be here in some capacity. So, this feels like their way of trying to figure things out. I would say the most surprise is probably Mike Dana. Dwayne Carter, third-round pick a couple years ago. I thought the writing was on the wall because of him being out on the field at the end of the game in the preseason finale. I wonder if that was a player that they were trying to trade and they just couldn't get something done, right? But they also just didn't feel good about cutting upright or straightforward a third-round pick from a few years ago coming off >> I would say they also might have just wanted to give him more reps because he was still he's still getting back from the injury. It was his last chance to kind of get on the field before week one, right? >> Yeah, and it's valid. And once again, like there is often a disconnect between what the front office is thinking and maybe what we're seeing. We're allowed to watch every practice for the most part during this portion of the schedule, but we don't see the walk-throughs and we're not going through some of the different things that they are looking for. So, like yeah, I thought Dwayne Carter was at real risk of potentially getting cut. There is a there's a tight end question I want to get to later, so I'm just going to kind of mark it here because I do think that's a really good question. But we'll we'll stay on the defensive line now. And Mike Dana, you at the beginning of the preseason seemed higher on Mike Dana than I did. Like I know he's been a player who's been in the league for a while, so he's got a proven track record, but I'm surprised they kept that many outside linebacker edge rushers. That that's a lot to me. To me To me anyway. >> Me I agree that it felt to me like you'd keep five from one of those positions. I was thinking more interior, but I could have seen only five. The rotation's going to be interesting. If you want to go to a, you know, think about a game day roster looks like, and they're not all going to be active, right? I mean, Mike Dana's probably not going to be active. Um and then Dwayne Carter maybe not. I don't What What's the number of total D-linemen, interior and edge, that are active on game day? 10? 10 sounds right. You think they have 11 or 12? >> I would say it's probably 10. I would say we're probably seeing one of those defensive linemen inactive and one of those edge rushers inactive. That that's my assumption. >> All right. So, Zane Durant then, he goes to IR to return, and I can confirm that it is IR to return. He's not out for the year. So, that gives you 4 weeks with him. Vetarian Mathis gives you 3 weeks. The difference is, once Vetarian Mathis' suspension is over, you do have to make a decision on him. You can't keep him on a suspended list. They have to make a decision to activate him or release him, and then, you know, you could try to bring him back in the practice squad. With Zane Durant, they can kind of just play the long game here. He doesn't have to come back. He counts already as your one eight guys to return, but he could stay on IR all year if they feel like they have what they need right there. So, he kind of solves that issue, as I say. But I don't I don't know if this group is totally spoken for yet. If they grab somebody from another position, that might be the area where they release somebody, one of these linemen. >> See, I think it might be Lotulelei, but I agree with you. Like I don't think it would be crazy if it was Mike Dana, right? Because just hey, he's a veteran, and you think maybe you could just get him back on your practice squad, but you're totally right because they're definitely not going to have all of those guys active on game days. It is going to be a play a position where they rotate substantially. The thing I don't understand or I should say probably surprised me a little bit was what we've seen from Zane Durant made it feel like and what I don't know exactly what the injury is. It made it feel like he was a guy who could come in and play and contribute. >> Yeah, I agree. >> Usually this IR to start thing is almost like the redshirt year of like hey, we're going to and I don't know what the injury is. So I don't want to speculate too much, but that's kind of why I thought it made more sense for Jude Bowery. I just don't know what the Jude Bowery status was and I that's why I thought that. >> and then Zane Durant actually got injured right at the end of the Steelers preseason game, which is why we're not really sure. Nothing really We didn't get any updates on that or reports on it. >> No, we haven't had any access or availability since that time and we won't until Tuesday. So we'll hear from Joe Brady and we'll hear from Brandon Beane and I'm sure Brandon will go through the injury outlook for everybody including the guys who are just on the 53-man roster. I also do think this is an often overlooked part of this, but none of the guys who are injured landing on IR or PUP like the notable guys is a very good sign for the Bills, right? If you were worried about the outlook of a C.J. Gardner-Johnson or a Keanu Neal or a Khalil Shakir or a Taron Johnson. None of those guys have any designation, which means the Bills think they'll all be ready to go at least very early on. The other one that I thought was sneaky and it wasn't like super sneaky was Connor McGovern. I was kind of waiting to see like is there a chance that they do something with McGovern because of what, you know, >> Well, I think the trade the trade that started the day kind of gave you a clue to that anyway. So there was a trade Cedric Van Pran Granger to the Indianapolis Colts and just so everybody knows, the Bills also send a seventh-round pick their own. They still have a Raiders seventh-round pick next year. They say they send Van Pran Granger and a seven to Indy for a six. You're right. You think about it kind of what it might look like, but then you trade Van Pran Granger, and you're like, "Okay, now you know McGovern's probably playing, and Lloyd Cushenberry, they're comfortable with him as the backup." Let's also remember Alec Anderson can play center, too, if they need him need him to. Excuse me, and Austin Corbett could play left guard in that situation. So, and he can play center, too. He can also play center if he needs to. That's right. I mean, heck, Bruno Fritsch could play center. I know he's you know, I know they waived him, but I mean, they have guys in the building who could do that. All right, let's get to what You want to go safety or linebacker or inside linebacker? Which one do you want to talk about? We got to wrap up the the defensive one of them. >> Inside linebacker is probably easier. I think the only surprise there was Jenkins, another player who I think will definitely be on the practice squad if they can. Um you know, this Joe Andreessen injury popped up at the beginning of this week, so we didn't know what his status was, but once again, the Bills must feel pretty comfortable there. >> Agreed. You know, K'Waun Williams Jenkins, we both spoke about him a lot where if the Bills wanted to keep five linebackers, he was on the team. If they wanted to keep four, he'd have to be over Joe Andreessen. And some people thought he might, and including because of Joe Andreessen's recent injury. The thing Joe Andreessen gives you, though, is besides being a really good special teams player, and he was second in the league last year in special teams tackles, he can play both positions. He can play Mike, he can play Will. But Buffalo Joe makes the squad again. Good for him. He's going into his third year. Of course, we know he had a tryout, undrafted rookie, undrafted free agent. He's going into his third year. Good for Joe Andreessen. He's on the team. And then you go to safety. Yes, folks, they kept five safeties. Let's remember, though, Sam Franklin really is not a safety. He's a strictly a special teams player. You're not playing him. And if you look at my list there, I would actually put Damar Hamlin is below is third on the list. This isn't a Yeah, this isn't a depth chart, so to speak, but if it was, Damar Hamlin's actually the third guy. And I I he's a very polarizing player to a lot of people. I'm going to say what I've always said about Damar Hamlin. Never going to wow you with plays, but it always seems like he's just in the right spot to kind of, you know, do his job. And that's what every team wants from a backup safety when they come in the game. >> Someone asked earlier who will be five inactives on game day be. I think we look at that safety room and I think one of them will come from that. I don't think it'll be Sam Franklin just because of the special teams role that he plays. I think the easy answer now will probably be Jaylen Kilgore. title: Colts Cover-2 Podcast: Keenan Allen arrested, Colts cut roster to 53
text: Hey there Colts fans. It's Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star. Joined here of course by my co-host Joel A Ericson. It is the Colts Cover Two podcast. We got a lot to break down today. Um, a lot of news around the Colts cuts to form their initial 53man roster with two weeks until the start of the 2026 season. And we also have some off the- field news to discuss as well that you probably have already read about. Kenan Allen, the Colts veteran wide receiver who was signed not even two weeks ago, just hours after making his onfield debut for the Colts in the preseason finale, was arrested early Sunday morning in downtown Indianapolis for suspicion of DUI. Um, we will let let's start there. Um, not the story that we were expecting to be covering this morning. Quite frankly, Joel and I both woke up a little after 7 a.m. Um, and saw that certainly you're surprised when you see a story like that about anyone. Um, I I think it was a little bit more so even that it was um, uh, frankly a veteran like Keenan Allen. Um, you you you don't want to see that from someone that I I feel like the Colts, even though he's been around the the team for less than two weeks, probably see as a a leader on this team. Um, you know, we we still know really, frankly, very little about what led to this. But what we do know, um, Kenan Allen arrested in the 1000 block of South Meridian Street on early Sunday morning around 1:00 am. He was um in his car, which was parked in a no parking zone um around 110 South Meridian Street. The police approached the car um when they realized it was parked where it was not supposed to be. And uh in speaking with Keenan began to uh suspect that he was under the influence. um in further investigation realized um that they suspected him of being over the legal limit, which in Indiana is 0.08% blood alcohol level. They then arrested him and charged him with operating motor a motor vehicle under the influence and um endangering a person. Those are two misdemeanor charges. He was uh booked into the uh Marian County Jail just south of downtown Indianapolis. He remained there for more than 12 hours. He was not released until I think it was 3:49 this afternoon. Um, and he now has a an upcoming hearing on September 16th, which is 3 days after when we would expect him to make his regular season debut for the Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium in week one against the Ravens. Um, I think those are all the the the facts that we know at the moment, Joel. um you've been covering the NFL for a long time. Just kind of give me your initial reaction to a story like this. Well, um I don't know, maybe this says something about what it's like when you about what the way the NFL works with this stuff, but like your first thought um when there's no report of an accident or something like that, like before we'd seen the police report, is honestly um what does this mean for his availability? >> Um I don't know that that is you know what you should think, but it's kind of the way it works in the NFL. I think it's probably where most fans heads went immediately was what you know what does this mean for his availability with the Colts. Um and pretty quickly like you know look we the NFL substance abuse policy which is what this falls under uh is readily available and publicly available online. I don't know if you do or don't know this, but it it was interesting to me how cut and dry it was laid out that hey, if you break the law um in an incident involving alcohol, even if it is your first time offense, this is what the penalty is going to be. It's going to be a three-game suspension. It's not, you know, for this charge it's a one game or this could be a two or or even leaving it undefined to kind of take it by on a case- by case basis. It is very cut and dry. If you um essentially if you drive uh or or behind the wheels of a vehicle under the influence and you are pulled over and you are arrested, um this is what the penalty is. And so, uh, as as you mentioned there, um, the the more that we found out researching some similar cases to this over the last couple years, um, that have all been three games, um, the NFL has clearly taken a very consistent policy on these in that they let all of these cases play through, uh, you kind of work their way through the justice system. This is not a situation where they will make a judgment on someone before they are found guilty or not guilty. This is these these are not the types of uh charges where the NFL is going to place you on the commissioner's exempt list like we've had some players here um in the last 24 hours or so. Um it that's that's not to say it's not a um a serious issue. anyone driving put, you know, getting behind the wheel while uh intoxicated is is a serious offense. But in the grand scheme of things, um rather than making a judgment when maybe not all the facts are available, um the the NFL takes a pretty concrete precedent of letting this all go through the court system. And sometimes uh I mean frankly often times when you look at the recent similar cases like this either players plead guilty to lesser offenses lesser offenses than they were initially charged with or they plead no contest um charges can be dropped sometimes.
