So Aaron Donald, which >> not yesterday, >> which that one's not injury related, but like come on. Uh Jaden Daniels plus 750 also looks pretty good. Yeah, if the commanders can get it together at all, we will talk tomorrow, assuming that the spectre of JJ McCarthy does not devour our uh essences. Good night.

title: GM Jon-Eric Sullivan meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Just to touch on the two quarterbacks acquired first, if you would mind going over each of them. McCord, what intrigued you about his skill set? And same obviously with Brady Book. >> Sure, I'll start with McCord. You know, I've always been a fan of his. I feel like when you watch the kid play, he's a he's a keep the train on the tracks kind of guy. Think he processes the game quick. I think I think he throws an an accurate catchable football. He runs the offense, you know, and and I know he's a smart guy. I know he's a competitive guy. Scouted him in college. Obviously followed him, tracked him through the preseason. And I thought he had opportunity coming here and and you know, we obviously want number two out there, but if something happened, I thought he could he could run the offense and help us give us a chance to win games. >> Did you think you would get seven? >> I did not. Um but I'm glad that we did. You know, I did not. You know, you never know how that's going to go. You're a little bit at the mercy of the football gods, if you will. But you know, I think we got incrementally better, which is always the goal. You guys know we're always going to turn this thing and and keep this thing rolling in terms of roster development and and competition. So I'm I'm glad we did what we did and I think we got a little bit better today. >> So we have our 53-man roster usually makes a statement about a program or about a team. What does this 53-man roster say about the 2026 Dolphins? >> Yeah, it's a good question. I think it says that we are we look at at ourselves honestly and that any chance we get to get better, we're going to get better. We are not going to tell ourselves lies when when things aren't getting done at the level that they need to get done and we're going to continually you know, turn over rocks to get better at every turn, you know, and I think I'm proud of our guys, all the guys that participated in camp. I think we got a lot of really think good things going. Very, very happy with our draft class as a whole. Certainly not here to anoint anyone that hasn't played an NFL game yet. But I do [clears throat] think those guys are are what we thought they would would be and I think that the vets that we brought in obviously some made it and some didn't. But uh I'm happy with where we are, but there is always room for growth. >> What can you tell us about the uh competition between Jacob Rodriguez and Gerald Datsun? And did Datsun at any point maybe even ask for his release rather than be a backup? Was any of that >> No, T Datsun pro. He he competed and um you know, I think it was a it was a fair competition. Um obviously we have a lot of like for Jacob Rodriguez. That's never been a a secret. Um I thought T Datsun showed up. He was a pro. He competed. Um it's a very fair question like why would you move on from T Datsun with with but I think it really just highlights how we feel about the young guys on our team. Um it's unfortunate what happened to Trey Moore. He will be back. Um we got a lot of like for for Jacob and and so on and so forth. Ronnie's done a good job and I you know, there's so many factors that go into when you're cutting the 53 down. It's layered. Uh both long-term, short-term. Um there's financial components. However, you you know, there's all kinds of things that go into the decisions. Um but we are very appreciative of what T Datsun has done here. I wish him nothing but the best. I'm sure he's going to go on and have a good career. Um he was very professional in our in our conversation. I wish I got nothing but the best. >> What was it like to strike a deal with your old boss, Brian Gutekunst? [clears throat] >> It was It was kind of cool, you know, to be honest with you. It was It was easy. Uh he knows me. I know him. We know how each other think and it was it was really kind of right to the point and uh he thought it was good for the Packers. I thought it was good for the Dolphins and we did what we did. >> So, you heard about what you said about McCord being able to come in here and run the offense. However, he hasn't been here that long and so if you know, Malik Willis got hurt against the Raiders, um what gives you confidence that McCord or or any of the other quarterbacks can come in here and run the offense? >> Bobby Slowik, Bush Hamdan. You know, they're good coaches. They'll get them ready. It's not ideal. I'm not going to sit up here in front of you try to say like this scenario is is perfect. It's not. I think sometimes when you're when you're talking about your roster and trying to get better, you have to take some chances and do some things that maybe are uncomfortable, if you will. But I have a lot of faith in the guys that are going to be coaching him every day and and you know, like I said, we hope we hope number two's out there, but if if something happens, I think we'll be ready to roll. >> When it comes to Quinn Ewers, I think we all saw that he struggled in camp. Knowing that he was dealing with a couple injuries, did that make it any more difficult of a decision or were you pretty set on what you wanted to do? >> At the time, you know, when I when I made the decision, I was set. And you know, again, no different than T-Bob, wish wish Quinn the best. And think Quinn has an opportunity to play in this league for a while and do well. I think he needed a fresh start. I think we needed a fresh start and I just think it Look, this is a performance-based business. And it was it was not getting done at the level that it needed to get done at. Quinn knew that. We had a lot of conversations. I think Quinn, if he was standing right here, would tell you that. You know, I just think it was time to kind of move on. Him get another fresh fresh start and us start fresh with somebody else as well. >> Going back to what Arkins just asked you regarding the quarterbacks, I would kind of broaden the question as a follow-up. Um you have so many new faces. >> Mhm. >> At what point do you have almost too many new faces to get ready for a season opener? >> I mean, look, this is the National Football League. You know, you hope everybody is is is professional, but it's really it's always about getting better. If you deem something not good enough, um then you have to address it. It's my job to make sure that we are uh as competitive as we can be in the moment given the circumstances and if we sit on our hands so that it's comfortable then I'm not doing my job as a general manager. Um I understand the question but you know we are where we are. You guys understand the circumstances and the things that we had to do you know we're a unique spot. Uh we had to do some things in the spring that are you know unprecedented and and so there's cause and effect everything you do but my job is to make sure that we keep getting better and I feel like we've we've done the best that we can in the situation we are in. >> Were there a few spots where you had to make a call with a longer lens after engaging in conversation with coaches who perhaps felt hey this guy or two can maybe help us a little more this year. >> Sure. Tell me about the lens. >> Yeah there's always a balance to that you know now versus down the road and and I have to be fair to the coaches and I have so much respect for my dad you guys know my dad's a coach I have so much respect for them and I think often times it's funny we laugh coaches you know coaches usually see things this far in front of their face and they should that's their job like they got to go out and win on Sunday it's my job to see the overview long-term big picture and you try to marry that up and balance we have got really really good relationships with these guys we have great conversations so I try to walk that line of doing what I need to do to make sure that we're getting better but by the same time same at the same time excuse me respecting the job that they have to do as well. >> What are your thoughts on Brady Cook and then you have Joe Tryon which [clears throat] is fine. If you could assess what what you liked about Brady Cook. >> Yeah Brady's the ultimate competitor tough as tough as nails got a lot of a lot of swag if you will guys follow him you watch what he did at Missouri in his time there and he elevated a a program that you know maybe at the time wasn't the most talented and they they played well and I think a lot of that had to do with him and I think again it just I think it upgraded our room. And again, I I have nothing but respect for Cam, Quan. I wish those guys the best. I think they'll play in this league. Um but I felt like we needed to turn a couple pages and and get better in there. Get get better performance and production. >> So, with the decision to trade Tutu and go so young at at wide receiver with the initial 53, is that sort of in line with your thoughts at at linebacker that it's just a reflection of how you feel about your young players? >> Yeah, I I mean, I think that's fair. I mean, you guys know, I've said it time and time again, we're going to be a draft and develop team. Obviously, we've only had one draft. Now, it's the best player available and that's just the way that it fell. You know, I didn't go into the draft like, "Hey, we got to revamp the receiver room or revamp the inside linebacker room." That's just the way that it fell in the moment. We felt like those guys were the best player on on the board at the time. Um but yeah, we'll be a draft and develop team. We will always be a young team. We will You guys know how to eat I've said it before, we will be very very selective in who we bring in here in free agency and we'll pay our core players. We just did that, you know, with with Jay Brooks and A chain and and and Brew. Um but that's how we'll move. So, we you know, I just I think this is a young man's game. I think from a salary cap standpoint, staying young allows you to be sustainable and then you go pay your your difference makers versus having a bunch of mercenaries that are paid that you know, overpaid if you will. >> So, with any special teams in general and Bradley Pinion specifically, did [clears throat] anybody make the roster based largely on special teams? Maybe DJ Harmon or someone and Bradley Pinion, are you comfortable with where he is after some hiccups in in preseason? >> Yeah, Brad I had a conversation with Bradley today. Um I have confidence and faith in Bradley. He knows he didn't have the best preseason or it was up and down anyway. He did actually a lot of good things. He just wasn't as consistent as he needs to be and and he would again, he would tell you that if he was standing right here. Uh you know, Ryan Miller I thought did some really good things as a coverage player. You know, that's why he's here on the 53. We needed you know, you get you always have to get those back in corner DB receiver spots. You got to get special teams play out of those guys. And so I if you're asking me to highlight one guy I'd say Ryan is a guy that I'm excited about and what he brought to the table in in the short time that he was with us from a special teams standpoint. >> What did you see out of Justin Jolly that wanted you to bring him in? >> Yeah, so we you know, we're banged up in that room a little bit and we we had a lot of like for him quite frankly. A lot of it was just based on our college evaluation of him. And so we'll bring him in and see see how he does and what it looks like and and move down the road with him. But to be honest with you that was basically based on the North Carolina State eval. >> When you watched the joint practices and you watched preseason games and watched training camp, what if anything do you feel you learned about the state of the team and the program? >> Sure, I feel like for for the better positive you want to focus on the positive. I thought we compete really hard. You know, I think um the effort, the the resilience, the physicality I think is there. I think again when you're playing a lot of young players, maybe the consistency is not what it needs to be yet. And then you know, I think there's there's places like every roster in the NFL where the depth is not what it needs to be. But you know, again my job to keep turning over rocks and and make sure that we're trying to fortify this roster that at every opportunity that we can. But you know, I think any any you know, even the good teams will sit up here and tell you hey, we got a room or two that it's not where it needs to be. We're no different. Maybe a little more significant than others. But we'll get there. >> Sully, it seems like there's like a higher volume of trades at least in recent see obviously here and elsewhere. I'm curious in your time how you maybe seen the trend of front offices being willing to trade uh change. >> Yeah, I think it's just um an effort to get better. You know, I think I think it's one of those deals where when you're looking at your roster and you see an opportunity to uh improve, then you you explore every avenue. And um and if if you deem it good for your team and and like there's different in the business, people view trading differently. You know, I'm I love picks. I come from a place that values draft picks. There's other places that have been very successful that don't value them as much. I'm not here to say who's right or who's wrong, but uh but I do think what we all share in common is just the effort and desire to get better. And when it is your job to make sure that that happens, um I think you have to take that serious. You have a huge responsibility. It's a very competitive league. We all know that and it's 1% better is 1% better and that's a huge deal when you're competing against the best in the world every Sunday. >> You know, [snorts] maybe outside the building, me personally, fans may like think trades are fun. Do you find that process fun for you trying to work with another team on maybe holes they have, you have, vice >> Depends on who you're dealing with. Um yeah, it's fun. You know, I think you know, it's it's the NFL. Being involved in the NFL is exciting. You know, that part of it's fun. Uh and I think anytime you're on the cusp of doing what you deem uh is is is an improvement to your roster is is fun. So. >> With Jacquizz Hunter, uh you traded for him in the 22 trade. Obviously, he's on your practice squad now. What did you see in him that made him a piece that you wanted? >> Yeah, Jacquizz is, you know, really back to his days in college. He's just a he's a hard-charging, very physical runner um that I feel like uh embodies what we want to be here, the physical, you know, run first, how you guys build the line of scrimmage, all that stuff. But he gets downhill, gets the tough yards. Wanted to get him here, wasn't sure how it would work out at the 53 cut, if we would carry him through or put him on the practice squad. There's so many moving parts, but definitely wanted him to be in the fold. And so, uh you know, 2-2, love the guy, probably was not going to going to make it. So, it was just an opportunity to uh to get him back to a spot where he had a better chance and and bringing a guy that we had some like for. >> Solly, two players that I'm wondering if you can, without giving away strategy, tell me their uh outlook for 2026. Willie Gay, is he a candidate to start early and how big is special teams for him? And then Kyle Lewis, is he kind of a I guess a a Swiss Army knife for lack of a better term? >> Yeah, Kyle is a Swiss Army knife and I, you know, our expectation for him, I think he'll be a really good special teams player. You know, you I'm sure you guys have seen we've had him out there doing some things that he's never done before as a gunner. And he's, you know, he's really good getting off the ball. He runs well. Um there's some things he's learning coming to balance. I mean, our our expectation is that while Kyle grows as a positional player, which he'll be kind of that what we call the the joker, the big nickel, and safety. Um that he will be a a difference maker for us on special teams. You know, that's his role early. Kyle's He's a really good football player and uh we expect him to do good things for us. And then Willie, you know, Willie's physical. Uh he can run. Special teams is vitally important to him. You know, right now we're banged up in the linebacker room. So, you know, it's it's hard to say if he'll, you know, where he'll land on the depth chart. You know, that's still in flux, but uh but we're glad Willie's on the team. Um you know, I thought he played with great effort and you always can see his speed and his running hit play style. And and you know, we'll kind of see how it unfolds with the other guys in the room. >> Solly, what's your assessment on how Proctor has made the adjustment to guard? >> I think he's done a nice job. Uh you know, the traits are what jump out to you. I think there's times um maybe with his eyes, you know, he could be a little better and cleaner, but but I yeah. Caden has done a great job. You know, we we watch practice every day and he continues to grow and turn corners and improve. Um is he all the way there yet? No. Do I expect him to be a really good player in the future? I do. I think he's doing a really good job. You know, the physicality is is you guys have heard me say it probably to the point of nauseam, but when he gets thick on people and moves people off the ball, it looks different than everybody else and he's he presents Malik with a very firm pocket. Guys cannot play through him. And you know, that's why we drafted him. The other stuff is all coachable and he will get better in time. >> Sorry about that. I was going to ask you on Chris Bell, did he exceed your expectations dramatically health-wise? And the top five this year potentially if your three draft picks, Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, do you feel good about that group this year? >> I do. I will start with Chris. Chris has worked his behind off to get himself ready. You know, our expectation was him probably getting him back after the bye. Uh it's a testament to the kid uh and it is also a testament to the people that work with with him every day. Kyle Johnston, Todd Hunt and and that staff down there. Um but yeah, we're excited about Chris. He's put forth the effort to get himself ready to go much earlier than we expected and you know, we'll get him going. Um >> Yeah, and the three rookies, Malik and Tolbert, that group. Obviously Miller you mentioned as well. >> Yeah. >> Feel good about that group being NFL quality receivers when some of them are so young? >> Yeah, the youth is the youth. You know, that that you you can't rush that. It is what it is. I mean, they'll they'll be inconsistencies. I I feel really good about the talent in the room. I feel like we need to continue to grow and evolve. We need to be more consistent, but I feel like we have NFL players in that room that should be good NFL players. Caleb, I mean, you guys are out there. Caleb has a lot of natural gifts and that's easy. You don't have to be a scout to see that. It shows itself every day. Caleb needs to be more consistent. Um you know, Malik Washington is a really good football player. He shows up every day. I'm glad we got him. I think Kevin Coleman has showed speed, twitch, hands, all the things that you want to see in a young receiver. Uh, you know, when I watch Kevin, that guy's an NFL football player. Um, what his ceiling is, we'll see. I don't have a crystal ball, but I've never for 1 second doubted that like he doesn't belong. I would actually say the opposite. He's exceeded expectations. And then Chris Bell's different, man. Guy's 220 lb to 228 lb 230 lb and and can run and powerful and he's just coming off an injury and we'll see, you know, we'll see where it goes, but I think all those guys are to this point what we expected. >> I wanted to ask about quarterback development and kind of in general what your approach and philosophy has been to finding and developing a young quarterback and kind of how you've seen league-wide that has changed um, in the last few years. >> Yeah, I mean, what I come from is uh, you you bring I don't think you can ever have enough quarterbacks. I mean, obviously the roster limitations prevent you from hoarding too many numbers, but I think you always want to try to get young quarterbacks that you think have the potential to grow. Uh, you want to get them in the stable and then you want to you want to try to develop them. I think processing is the most important thing, the ability to play quick between the ears. Um, I love arm strength. I love athleticism, but if you can process the game and play quick and then you can throw an accurate catchable ball, I think you have a chance to play in this league. Um, I come from a place that when you have a chance to sit, obviously you guys know in in Green Bay, you know, I was there and we had Brett and drafted Aaron. He sat for 3 years where he could watch Brett every day, get coached up and then when it came his time, he was ready to go here. He was confident. He was he knew what he was looking at and he could play fast. And then we did the same thing with Jordan. And so, you know, you take a Kyle, you take a Brady Cook, um, you take those guys and let them sit behind Malik for a couple years and and you know, if you feel like you got a guy, then you you know, you either trade him or something happens to Malik. You know, who knows what the future holds, but I think when those guys that you believe in and look, they won't all work out. They won't all I mean that's just the truth. Draft picks, guys that you bring in, they're not going to all work out. Um but I think when you feel like people have talent, especially quarterbacks, you bring them in, you coach them up, you let it simmer and then you see what you got down the road. >> You see him up on a line of this quarterback development question. You talk about the youth that you have here. How do you get a long-term eval of Malik when there's maybe moving chairs, maybe some chemistry things you have to continue to work with through the season? >> Yeah, it's a great question. Um >> [clears throat] >> I think it's, you know, I think anytime you're your ability to move the football, your ability to handle the hard times as as a guy, your ability to process. I mean, Malik I think is different than most because of the athletic traits he has, the powerful arm. I feel very comfortable that as these young players grow with Malik, you'll we'll all see what Malik is. the evaluation part of it is just simply playing the position soundly, you know, making good decisions, using your legs when you need to use your legs, throwing the ball accurately, getting the ball out on time, processing. Um I know where you're going with the question. It's like, do we have enough around him for us to evaluate him? I would say yes, we do. Um but I don't know that you guys will see it the way we see it when we're evaluating. Does that make sense? I don't know that the fans, the common fan that's sitting out there is going to watch what's going on and say, this guy's got a chance to be a really good player. Maybe they will. Um maybe they won't, but I think we'll be able to measure that uh each weekend and week out and see if he's going this way. >> Is there something that we should be looking at? I don't know, we don't have your scout eye, but is there something that we should be looking at in signs of, hey, this guy's got it long-term based on this. >> Yeah, I mean, I to me it's one of those things that you don't overcomplicate it. Like it you know, is he is he making good decisions? Is he taking care of the ball? Is he taking care of the ball? Is he turning the ball over? I mean, you can't win the if you're a running back, you can't fumble. If you're quarterback, you can't throw interceptions. Like you cannot turn the ball over and win in this league. I think um is he throwing the ball accurately? You know, is he missing guys? Is he using his legs when he should use his legs? That's one of his greatest gifts. I mean, I think I don't think you you know, and then and are we moving the ball? Is he making you know, I think they're really good when it's tilt the field in their favor. Maybe when everything around him is not ideal, you know, uh and and I think he has that kind of ability. Now, time will tell, but I I think you'll see a player in Malik that has a lot of uh traits and then and then intangibles that will allow him to be successful in this league. >> So, you know, you guys are process-oriented over results-oriented, but is there an exception at edge rusher? Do you need to see some quarterback on the ground numbers in the form of sacks? >> Especially with Chop. >> Starting with Chop. >> Yeah, Chop, you know, I I I have big expectations for Chop. I think Chop has had a really good camp. Um I think he's an ascending player. So, sure. Yeah, I mean, we need we need pass rush. Every NFL team needs pass rush. I would say Chop is our most gifted pass rusher. I don't think that's a secret. Um but we need Chop to answer the bell and and keep keep doing the things that he's doing. Keep turning corners and and get and get bunch of sacks for us. Any team's going to benefit from that. Uh I think half and and those guys, you know, I think right now we got a bunch of rugged, tough edge setters. I think we're going to have to scheme up pass rush. Um but I think Ooch and and and and those guys are up to the challenge. And Ooch, like when you watch Ooch, he's got he's got very natural pass rush ability. Um he is quick, he's slippery, and then that's when the coaches come in and and and they draw it up and get you home. but uh but I did to answer your question, I'm excited about Shop. You know, I think those other guys are all role players. They know they're role players, but but I'm glad that they're here. I think they've gone about it the right way. I think they're rugged, tough guys and and we'll see what we can come up with. >> Just a quick follow-up again on the the quarterback thing. There seems to be like a carousel of of quarterbacks um with teams not, you know, if finding out if that's their guy or not. I know this varies from team to team, but what are the factors and how patient you can be in figuring out if this is your guy for the future? >> Level of play, you know, and and then look, we're always we're in this business to win. You know, I think any any quarterback, any head coach, any general manager, at the end of the day you're going to be judged on wins and losses. That doesn't fall short on me. Like nobody cares your circumstances, what you've had to over Nobody cares. You're winning or you're losing. So ultimately with Malik, with myself, with half, we're going to be judged on wins and losses. I think with with Malik in particular, any quarterback, I again, I think it's I always start with the uh I always start with the ability to to to play the game at a high level and that's just processing the game um taking care of the ball, not turning the ball over, and then making plays when they're when they are there to be had, you know, um we've all seen those quarterbacks that sit in there and they you got a guy run across the middle and they overshoot him. Like we you know, you can't do that time and time and time again. You got to make the throws you're supposed to make. You got to make the runs you're supposed to make. You got to make the reads you're supposed to make and just play the game at a high level that gives your chance or your team a chance to win every week. And I think that's the big the big key is the consistency. You can't be up and down and up and down. You can't win that way. You got to be consistent every week. That's not to say you won't make mistakes. You will, but then you got to bounce back at a high level. >> So you made a strong investment in A chain and he's talked about wanting the ball, wanting the responsibility. That's a lower shelf life position. How do you balance maybe getting your investment in that position with this year or you know, the touches may not be as important long term for how you view this team? >> Yeah, so I mean I just want to make sure I'm answering your question. You're say you're saying like how do we preserve his health and get him his touches? Okay. >> three, four years from now he's still a really good player for you guys. >> Sure. I mean, you know, that's where Jaylen Wright and Ali got to step up. You know, those guys both have a skill set. You know, Jaylen's a big back that can gash. He can you know, fast. You know, he can he can crease you. Ali's a big back with tremendous hands and and you know, got power and size. And we need to use those guys. We got to be able to depend on those guys. And so I think you know, A&M is a special player. We all know that. He's going to get the ball. He's going to touch the ball. We have to be creative in how we get him his touches. But but the other two got to step up so that we have faith in those guys to spell A&M and feel like we you know, we don't drop off. You know, and I I think both those guys are very very capable. >> Most NFL starts of anyone in your secondary is Deuce Vaughn's 11. We talked about this a little bit in April, but how much have you given thought to do we have enough veteran experience proven NFL starters at safety and corner and how did you arrive at the decision to go with almost entirely youth there? >> Yeah, I mean it it's part of it's just who performed at the highest level in camp. Who who we felt like yeah I look, it crosses my mind. Like we haven't we don't have a ton of experience in the room. But I like who we have in the room. I think we have guys that are competitive and and can play the game. But then you know, they got to step up. They have a responsibility and you know, we're going to get tested here in a couple weeks and we'll see where it goes, but uh Yeah, I mean we're young. You know, I don't I mean if you're looking for me to I don't there it is what it is. You know, we're young. We're inexperienced. There's going to be some growing pains, but but we'll we'll lean on each other and we'll get through it and I expect those guys to grow every week as players. >> So you have some exciting young talent at D-tackle. I'm wondering what the approach was with Zeke Biggers. I'm not sure that he played in games. How did he look in in joint practices and inter-squad practices? >> Yeah, Zeke's done a really good job and he's he's provided some versatility. He can play inside as a D-tackle. He can play big end. Zeke is a guy that over time I've really really grown with in terms of my confidence and and my belief in him. He plays hard. He's physical. He's got length. It's important to him to be a good player. I think he think he approaches the game the right way. He was dealing with a couple little minor things which is you know why you guys didn't see him out there at times in games but but I'm I'm very pleased with Zeke and I think he's going the right way as a football player and I think he's going to provide us some versatility across that D-line both big end and D-tackle.

title: General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: I thought he had opportunity coming in here and and uh we obviously want number two out there, but if something happened, I thought he could he could run the offense and help us uh give us a chance to win games. >> Did you think you would get seven? >> I did not. Um, but I'm glad that we did. You know, I did not. You You never know how that's going to go. Uh, you're a little bit at the mercy of the football gods, if you will. But, uh, you know, I think we got incrementally better, which is always the goal. Uh, you guys know we're always going to churn this thing and and keep this thing rolling in terms of roster development and and competition. So, I'm I'm glad we did what we did, and I think we got a little bit better today. >> So, a 53man roster usually makes a statement about a program or about a team. What does this 53man roster say about the 2026 conference? >> Yeah, it's a good question. I think it says that we are uh we look at it ourselves honestly and that any chance we get to get better, we're going to get better. Um we are not going to tell ourselves lies when when uh things aren't getting done at the level that they need to get done. And we're going to continually um you know turn over rocks to get better at every turn, you know. And I think I'm proud of our guys, all the guys that participated in camp. I think we got a lot of really think good things going. Very, very happy with our draft class as a whole. Um, certainly not here to anoint anyone that hasn't played an NFL game yet, but I [clears throat] do think those guys are are what we thought they would be. And I think that the vets that we brought in, obviously, some made it and some didn't, but I'm happy with where we are, but there is always room for growth. What can you tell us about the uh competition between Jacob Rodriguez and Terrell Dodson? And did Dodson at any point maybe even ask for his release rather than be a backup? Was any of that? >> No, T do D's a pro. He he competed and um you know, I think it was a it was a fair competition. Um obviously we have a lot of like for Jacob Rodriguez. That's never been a secret. Um, I thought T dot showed up. He was a pro. He competed. Um, it's a very fair question like why would you move on from T Dot with with but I think it really just highlights how we feel about the young guys on our team. Um, it's unfortunate what happened to Trey Moore. He will be back. Um, we got a lot of like for for Jacob and and so on and so forth. Ronnie's done a good job and you know there's so many factors that go into when you're cutting the 53 down. It's layered uh both long-term, shortterm. Um there's financial components. However you you know there's all kinds of uh things that go into the decisions. Um but we are very appreciative of what T dot has done here. I wish him nothing but the best. I'm sure he's going to go on and have a good career. Um he was very professional in our in our conversation. I wish that guy nothing but the best. >> What was it like to strike a deal with your old boss [clears throat] Good? >> It was it was kind of cool, you know, to be honest with you. It was it was easy. Uh he knows me, I know him, we know how each other think, and it was it was really kind of right to the point. and uh he thought it was good for the Packers. I thought it was good for the Dolphins and we did what we did. >> So, I heard about what you said about Rour being able to come in here and run the offense. However, he hasn't been here that long and so if you know Malik Willis got hurt against the Raiders. Um what gives you confidence that McCord or or any of the other quarterbacks could come in here and run the offense? >> Bobby Sloick, Bush Hampton, you know, they they're good coaches. They'll get them ready. It's not ideal. I'm not going to sit up here in front of you and try to say like this scenario is is perfect. It's not. Um I think sometimes when you're when you're talking about your roster and trying to get better, you have to take some chances and do some things that maybe are uncomfortable, if you will. But I have a lot of faith in the guys that are going to be coaching him every day. And and uh you know, like I said, we hope we hope number two's out there, but uh if if something happens, uh I think we'll be ready to roll. When >> it comes to Quinn Y, I think we all saw that he struggled in camp. uh knowing that he was dealing with a couple injuries, did that make it any more difficult of a decision or were you pretty set on what you wanted to do? >> Uh at the time, you know, when I when I made the decision, I was set and you know, again, no different than T dot. Wish wish wish Quinn the best and think Quinn has an opportunity to play in this league for a while and do well. I think he needed a fresh start. Um I think we needed a fresh start and I just think it uh look, this is a performance-based business. U and it was it was not getting done at the level that it needed to get done at. Quinn knew that. We had a lot of conversations. I think Quinn, if he was standing right here, would tell you that. Um, you know, I just think it was time to kind of move on, him get another fresh fresh start and us start fresh with somebody else as well. >> Going back to what Perkins just asked you regarding the quarterbacks, I would kind of broaden the question as a followup. Um, you have so many new faces. >> At what point do you have almost too many new faces to get ready for a season opener? I mean, look, this is the National Football League. You know, you hope everybody is is is professional, but it's really it's always about getting better. If you deem something not good enough, um, then you have to address it. It's my job to make sure that we are as competitive as we can be in the moment given the circumstances. And if we sit on our hands so that it's comfortable, then I'm not doing my job as a general manager. Um, I understand the question, but uh, you know, we are where we are. You guys understand the circumstances um, and the things that we had to do. You know, we're in a unique spot. Uh, we had to do some things in the spring that are, you know, unprecedented and and so there's cause and effect everything you do, but my job is to make sure that we keep getting better. and I feel like we've we've done the best that we can in the situation that we are in. >> There are a few spots where you had to make a call with a longer lens after engaging in conversation with coaches who perhaps felt, hey, this guy or two could maybe help us a little more this year. Sure. >> Tell me about the lens. >> Yeah, there's always a balance to that, you know, now versus down the road. And and I have to be fair to the coaches. Um, and I have so much respect. My dad, you guys know my dad's a coach. I have so much respect for them. And I think oftentimes, it's funny, we laugh, coaches, you know, coaches usually see things this far in front of their face and they should. That's their job. Like they got to go out and win on Sunday. It's my job to see the overview, long-term, big picture. And you try to marry that up and balance. We have got really really good relationships with these guys. We have great conversations. Um, so I I try to walk that line of doing what I need to do to make sure that we're getting better, but by the same time uh same at the same time, excuse me, respecting the job that they have to do as well. to Brady Cook. I know Joey jumped in, which [clears throat] is fine. Uh if you could assess what what you liked about Brady Cook. >> Yeah, Brady's the ultimate competitor. Tough as tough as nails. Um got a lot of a lot of swag, if you will. Guys follow him. You watch what he did at Missouri and his time there and he elevated a a program that uh you know, maybe at the time wasn't the most talented. They they played well and I think a lot of that had to do with him. And I think again it just I think it upgraded our room. And again, I have nothing but respect for Cam, Quinn. I wish those guys the best. I think they'll play in this league. Um, but I felt like we needed to uh turn a couple pages and and get better in there, get get better performance and production. >> So, the decision to trade 22 and go so young at at wide receiver with the initial 53, is that sort of in line with your thoughts at at linebacker that it's just a reflection of how you feel about your young players? >> Yeah, I mean, I think that's fair. I mean, you guys know, I've said it time and time again, we're going to be a draft and develop team. Obviously, we've only had one draft. Now, it's best player available. And that's just the way that it fell. You know, I didn't go into the draft like, "Hey, we got to revamp the receiver room or revamp the inside linebacker room." That's just the way that it fell in the moment. We felt like those guys were the best player on uh on the board at the time. Um but yeah, we'll be a draft and develop team. We will always be a young team. We will, you guys know how I've said it before, we will be very very selective in who we bring in here in free agency and we'll pay our core players. We just did that, you know, with with Jay Brooks and Achain and and and Brew. Um, but that's how we'll move. So, we, you know, I just I think this is a young man's game. I think from a salary cap standpoint, staying young, uh, allows you to be sustainable and then you go pay your your difference makers, um, versus having a bunch of mercenaries that are paid that, you know, overpaid, if you will. So, we're going to special teams in general and Bradley Pinion specifically. Did [clears throat] anybody make the roster based largely on special teams? Maybe DJ Herman or someone. And Bradley Pinion, are you comfortable with where he is after some hiccups in in preseason? >> Yeah, Brad, I had a conversation with Bradley today. Um, I have confidence and faith in Bradley. He knows he didn't have the best preseason or it was up and down anyway. He did actually a lot of good things. He just wasn't as consistent as he needs to be. and he would again he would tell you that if he was standing right here. Uh you know Ryan Miller I thought did some really good things as a coverage player. You know that's why he's here on the 53. We needed you know you always have to get those backend corner DB receiver spots. You got to get special teams play out of those guys. Uh and so I if you're asking me to highlight one guy I'd say Ryan is a guy that I'm excited about and what he brought to the table in the short time that he was with us from a special team standpoint. >> What did you see out of Justin Jolly that wanted you to bring him in? >> Yeah. So, we, you know, were banged up in that room a little bit. Uh, and we we had a lot of like for him. Quite frankly, a lot of it was just based on our college, uh, evaluation of him. And so, we'll bring him in, see see how he does and what it looks like and and move down the road with him. But, to be honest with you, that was basically based on the North Carolina State Evo. When you watched the Joy practices and you watched pre-season games and you watched training camp, >> what if anything do you feel you learned about the state of the team and the program? >> Sure. I feel like uh for for the better positive, if you want to focus on the positive, I thought we compete really hard. you know, I think um the effort uh the the resilience uh the physicality I think is there. I think um again when you're playing a lot of young players, maybe the consistency is not what it needs to be yet. And then uh you know, I think there's there's places like every roster in the NFL where the depth is not what it needs to be. But, you know, again, my job to keep turning over rocks and and make sure that we're trying to fortify this roster at every opportunity that we can. But, you know, I think any any, you know, even the good teams to sit up here and tell you, hey, we got a room or two that it's not where it needs to be. We're no different. Um, maybe a little more significant than others, but uh but we'll get there. >> Sully, it seems like there's like a higher volume of trades, at least in recency, obviously here and elsewhere. I'm curious in your time how you maybe seen the trend of front offices being willing to trade uh change. >> Yeah, I think it's just um an effort to get better. You know, I think I think it's one of those deals where when you're looking at your roster and you see an opportunity to uh improve, then you you explore every avenue and um and if you deem it good for your team and and look there's different in the business, people view trading differently. You know, I'm I love picks. I come from a place that values draft picks. There's other places that have been very successful that don't value them as much. I'm not here to say who's right or who's wrong, but uh but I do think what we all share in common is just the effort and desire to get better. And when it is your job to make sure that that happens, um I think you have to take that serious. You have a huge responsibility. It's a very competitive league. We all know that. And it's 1% better is 1% better. And that's a huge deal when you're competing against the best in the world every Sunday. >> You [snorts] know, maybe outside the building, me personally, fans may like think trades are fun. Do you find that process fun for you trying to work with another team on maybe holes they have, you have vice versa? >> Depends on who you're dealing with. Um, yeah, it's fun. You know, I think, you know, it's it's the NFL being involved in the NFL is exciting. You know, that part of it is fun. Uh, and I think anytime you're on the cusp of doing what you deem, uh, is is is an improvement to your roster is is fun. So, >> with Jacquz Hunter, uh, you traded for him for in the 22 Outwell trade. Obviously, he's on your practice squad now. What did you see in him that made him a piece that you wanted? >> Yeah, Joz is, you know, really back to his days in college. He's just he's a hard charging very physical runner. Um that I feel like embodies what we want to be here. The physical, you know, run first. You guys build the line of scrimmage, all that stuff. But he gets downhill, gets the tough yards. Wanted to get him here. Wasn't sure how it would work out at the 53 cut if we would carry him through or put him on the practice squad. There's so many moving parts. But definitely wanted him to be in the fold. And so, uh, you know, 22, love the guy. Probably was not gonna gonna make it. So, it was just an opportunity to uh to get him back to a spot where he had a better chance and and bring in a guy that we had some like for >> s um two players that I'm wondering if you can without giving away strategy tell me their uh outlook for 2026. Willie Gay, is he a candidate to start early and how big is special teams for him? And then Kyle Lewis, is he kind of a I guess a Swiss Army knife for lack of a better term? Yeah, Kyle is a Swiss Army knife and I, you know, our expectation for him, I think he'll be a really good special teams player. You know, I'm sure you guys have seen, we've had him out there doing some things that he's never done before as a gunner and he's, you know, he's really good getting off the ball. He runs well. Um, there's some things he's learning coming to balance. I mean, but but our expectation is that while Kyle grows as a positional player, which will be kind of that what we call the the joker, the big nickel and safety, um that he will be a a difference maker for us on special teams. You know, that's his role early. Kyle's he's a really good football player and uh we expect him to do good things for us. And then Willie, you know, Willy's physical. Uh he can run special teams is vitally important to him. You know, right now we're banged up in the linebacker room. So, you know, it's it's hard to say if he'll, you know, where he'll land on the depth chart. You know, that's still in flux, but uh but we're glad Willy's on the team. Um you know, thought he played with great effort, and you always can see his speed and his run and hit play style, and you we'll kind of see how it unfolds with the other guys in the room. >> What's your assessment on how Proctor has made the adjustment to guard? >> I think he's done a nice job. Uh you know, the traits are what jump out to you. I think there's times um maybe with his eyes, you know, he could be a little better and cleaner, but but I yeah, Kaden has done a great job. You know, we watch practice every day, and he continues to grow and turn corners and improve. Um is he all the way there yet? No. Do I expect him to be a really good player in the future? I do. I think he's doing a really good job. you know, the physicality is his, you guys have heard me say it probably to the point of nauseium, but when he gets thick on people and moves people off the ball, it looks different than everybody else. And he's he presents Malik with a very firm pocket. Guys cannot play through him and uh you know, and that's why we drafted him. The other stuff is all coachable and he will get better in time. >> Sorry about that. I was going to ask you on Chris Bell, did he exceed your expectations dramatically healthwise and a top five this year potentially of your three draft picks? Malik Washington, Jaylen Tolbert. Do you feel good about that group this year? >> I do. Uh we'll I'll start with Chris. Chris has worked his behind off to get himself ready. You know, our expectation was him probably getting him back after the buy. Uh it's a testament to the kid. Uh and it is also a testament to the people that work with with him every day. Kyle Johnston, Todd Hunt, and and that staff down there. Um but yeah, we're excited about Chris. uh he's put forth the effort to get himself ready to go much earlier than we expected and uh you know we'll get him going. Um >> yeah and the three rookies Malik and Tolbert that group obviously Miller you mentioned as well >> uh feel good about that group being NFL quality receivers when some of them are so young. >> Yeah, the youth is the youth you know that that you you can't rush that. It is what it is. I mean they'll there'll be inconsistencies. I I feel really good about the talent in the room. I feel like we need to continue to grow and evolve. Uh we need to be more consistent. Um but I feel like we have NFL players in that room that uh should be good NFL players. Caleb, I mean, you guys are out there. Caleb has a lot of natural gifts. Um and that's easy. You don't have to be a scout to see that. It shows itself every day. Caleb needs to be more consistent. Um you know, Malik Washington is a really good football player. He shows up every day. I'm glad we got him. I think Kevin Coleman has showed speed, twitch, hands, all the things that you want to see in a young receiver. Uh, you know, when I watch Kevin, that guy's an NFL football player. Um, how what his ceiling is, we'll see. I don't have a crystal ball, but I've never for one second doubted that like he doesn't belong. I would actually say the opposite. He's exceeded expectations. And then Chris Bell is different, man. Guy's 220 lbs to 228 pounds, 230 lbs, and can run and powerful and he's just coming off an injury and we'll, you know, we'll see where it goes. But I think all those guys are to this point what we expected. >> I wanted to ask about quarterback development and kind of in general what your approach and philosophy has been to finding and developing a young quarterback and kind of how you've seen leaguewide that has changed um in the last few years. >> Yeah. I mean what I come from is uh you you bring I don't think you can ever have enough quarterbacks. I mean, obviously the roster limitations prevent you from hoarding too many numbers, but I think you always want to try to get young quarterbacks that you think have the potential to grow. Uh, you want to get them in the stable and then you want to you want to try to develop them. I think processing is the most important thing. The ability to play quick between the ears. Um, I love arm strength. I love athleticism, but if you can process the game and play quick and then you can throw an accurate catchable ball, I think you have a chance to play in this league. Um, I come from a place that when you have a chance to sit, obviously you guys know in Green Bay, you know, I was there when we had Brett and drafted air and he sat for three years where he could watch Brett every day, get coached up, and then when it came his time, he was ready to go here. He was confident. He was he knew what he was looking at and he could play fast. And then we did the same thing with Jordan. And so, you know, you take a Kyle, you take a Brady Cook. Um, you take those guys and let him sit behind Malik for a couple years and and you know, if you feel like you got a guy, then you you know, you either trade him or something happens to Malik, you know, who knows what the future holds. But I think when those guys that you believe in, and look, they won't all work out. They won't all I mean, that's just the truth. Draft picks, guys, they're not going to all work out. Um, but I think when you feel like people have talent, especially quarterbacks, you bring them in, you coach them up, you let it simmer, and you see what you got down the road. >> Up on Alana's quarterback development question. You talked about the youth that you have here. How do you get a long-term eval of Malik when there's maybe moving chairs, maybe some chemistry things you have to continue to work with through the season? >> Yeah, it's a great question. Um, [clears throat] I think it's, you know, I think anytime you, your ability to move the football, your ability to handle the hard times as a guy, your ability to process, I mean, Malik, I think, is different than most because of the athletic traits he has, the powerful arm. I feel very comfortable that as these young players grow with Malik, you'll we'll all see what Malik is. Um, the evaluation part of it is just simply playing the position soundly, you know, making good decisions, using your legs when you need to use your legs, throwing the ball accurately, getting the ball out on time, processing. Um, I know where you're going with the question. It's like, do we have enough around him for us to evaluate him? I would say yes, we do. Um, but I don't know that you guys will see it the way we see it when we're evaluating. Does that make sense? I don't know that the fans, the common fan that's sitting out there is going to watch what's going on and say, "This guy's got a chance to be a really good player." Maybe they will. Um, maybe they won't, but I think we'll be able to measure that uh each week in and week out and see if he's going this way. >> Is there something that we should be looking at? I don't know. We don't have your scout eye, but is there something that we should be looking at in signs of, hey, this guy's got it long term based on this? >> Yeah. I mean I to me it's one of those things that you don't over complicate it like you know is he is he making good decision is he taking care of the ball is he taking care of the ball is he turning the ball over I mean you can't win the if you're a running back you can't fumble if you're quarterback you can't throw interceptions like you cannot turn the ball over and win in this league I think um is he throwing the ball accurately you know is he missing guys uh is he using his legs when he should use his legs that's one of his greatest gifts I mean I think I don't think you know and then and are we moving the Paul is he make, you know, I think the really good ones tilt the field in their favor, maybe when everything around him is not ideal, you know, uh and and I think he has that kind of ability. Now, time will tell, but I I think you'll see a player in Malik that has a lot of uh traits and then and then intangibles that will allow him to be successful in this league. >> So, you know, you guys are processoriented over resultsoriented, but is there an exception at edge rusher? Do you need to see some quarterback on the ground numbers in the form of sex from that? Especially with Chop, starting with Chop. >> Yeah, Chop, you know, I I I have big expectations for Chop. I think Chop is had a really good camp. Um I think he is an ascending player. So, sure. Yeah. I mean, we need we need pass rush. Every NFL team needs pass rush. I would say Chop is our most gifted pass rusher. I don't think that's a secret. Um but we need Chop to answer the bell and and keep keep doing the things that he's doing. keep turning corners and and get and get bunch of sacks for us. [snorts] Any team's going to benefit from that. Uh I think Half and and those guys, you know, I think right now we got a bunch of rugged, tough edge setters. I think we're going to have to scheme up pass rush. Um but I think ooch and and and and those guys are up to the challenge. And oo, like when you watch, he's got he's got very natural pass rush ability. Um he is quick, he's slippery, and then that's when the coaches come in and and and they draw it up and get you home. But uh but I to answer your question, I'm excited about Chop. You know, I think those other guys are all role players. They know they're role players. Um but but I'm glad that they're here. I think they've gone about it the right way. I think they're rugged, tough guys and and uh we'll see what we can come up with. >> Just a quick followup again on the the quarterback thing. there seems to be like a carousel of of quarterbacks um with teams not you know if finding out if that's their guy or not. I know this varies from team to team, but what are the factors and how patient you can be in figuring out if this is your guy for the future? >> Level of play, you know, and then look, we're always we're in this business to win, you know. I think any any quarterback, any head coach, any general manager at the end of the day, you can be judged on wins and losses. That doesn't fall short on me. Like, nobody cares your circumstances, what you've had to over nobody. It's you're winning or you're losing. So ultimately with Malik, with myself, with Half, we're going to be judged on wins and losses. Um, I think with with Malik in particular or any quarterback, again, I think it's I always start with the uh I always start with the ability to to to play the game at a high level. And that's just processing the game. Um, taking care of the ball, not turning the ball over, and then making plays when they're when they are there to be had. you know, um we've all seen those quarterbacks that sit in there and they you got a guy running across the middle and they overshoot them like we, you know, you can't do that time and time and time again. You got to make the throws you're supposed to make. You got to make the runs you're supposed to make. You got to make the reads you're supposed to make and just play the game at a high level that gives your chance your team a chance to win every week. And I think that's the big the big key is the consistency. You can't be up and down and up and down. You can't win that way. You got to be consistent every week. That's not to say you won't make mistakes. you will, but then you got to bounce back at a high level. >> So, you made a strong investment in Han and he's talked about wanting the ball, wanting the responsibility. That's a lower shelf life position. How do you balance maybe getting your investment in that position with this year or uh you know, the touches may not be as important long term for how you view this team. >> Yeah. So, I mean, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question. You're say you're saying like how do we preserve his health and get him his touches? Okay. that three, four years from now, he's still a really good player for you guys. >> Sure. I mean, you know, that's where Jaylen Wright and Ali got to step up. You [clears throat] know, those guys both have a skill set. You know, Jaylen's a big back that can gash. He can, you know, fast. You know, he can he can crease you. Um Ali's a big back with tremendous hands and and uh you know, got power and size and we need to use those guys, but we got to be able to depend on those guys. Um and so I I think you know, Achain's a special player. We all know that. He's going to get the ball. He's going to touch the ball. We have to be creative in how we get him his touches. Uh but but the other two got to step up so that we have faith in those guys uh to spell a chain and feel like you know we don't drop off you know and I I think both those guys are very very capable. >> Most NFL starts of anyone in your secondaries [snorts] Brent 11. We talked about this a little bit in April, but how much have you given thought to do we have enough veteran experience, proven NFL starters at safety and corner and how did you arrive at the decision to go with almost entirely youth there? >> Yeah, I mean it's part of it is just who performed at the highest level in camp who who we felt like get I look it crosses my mind like we haven't we don't have a ton of experience in the room. Um but I like who we have in the room. Um, I think we have guys that are competitive and and can play the game. Um, but they, you know, they got to step up. They have a responsibility and, you know, we're going to get tested here in a couple weeks and we'll see where it goes. But, uh, yeah, I mean, we're young. You know, I don't I mean, if you're looking for me to, I don't, it is what it is. You know, we're young, we're inexperienced. There's going to be some growing pains, but uh, but we'll we'll lean on each other and we'll get through it. And I expect those guys to grow every week as players. So, you have some exciting young talent at DTackle. Uh, I'm wondering what the approach was with Zeke Biggers. I'm not sure that he played in games. How did he look in in joint practices and intra squad practices? >> Yeah, Zeke's done a really good job. Um, and he's he's provided some versatility. He can play inside as a DTackle. He can play big end. Um, Zeke is a guy that over time I've, you know, really really grown with in terms of my confidence and and my belief in him. Uh, he plays hard. He's physical. He's got length. Um it's important to him to be a good player. I think he I think he approaches the game the right way. Uh he was dealing with a couple little minor things uh which is, you know, why you guys didn't see him out there at times um in games, but uh but I'm I'm very pleased with Zeke and I think he's going the right way as a football player and I think he's going to provide us some versatility across that D line, both big end and dtackle. Thank you guys. Thank you. >> All right. Thank you guys. Y'all have a good one.

title: How Has Malik Willis Progressed Throughout Camp?
text: We had an idea of going into training camp, the battles, and what we wanted to see, and all that stuff. I will start and tell you if I think the team in my eyes is better than when training camp started. And to be honest with you, after all the stuff we've heard from Malik Willis, I will say this, Malik Willis has progressed for me, and uh I have a little bit more promise in Malik from when training camp started, cuz at first I was like, I don't know what he can do or he can't do. Now I'm seeing I like his mobility and all that stuff, but overall, the team, to me, I had five wins going into training camp. I'm still at five wins now. It's it's kind of everything's the same. Nothing They didn't really do anything to shock me be like, "Wow, oh my god, that area of the team is so much better." But not really say, "Wow, that area of the team is so much worse." So, for me, going into the season now, and again, I had low expectations. Again, five wins. Uh nothing's changed for me. I I think, you know, I'm kind of still in the same mindset. Um >> Let's go with TD. I'm going to switch it around. TD. >> I would like to follow up with these questions for you because you alleged nothing has gotten worse than what you expected. So, did you expect quarterback to be this bad from a backup standpoint? >> Yeah. I did. >> You did? Uh safety as far as fitting the run a few times. Um found some opportunities in special teams to contribute. And so um you know, those are tough decisions. Uh Tanner's a kicker in this league. Charlie's a kicker in this league. I think we had uh some really good good guys there. Yes. >> On uh Mike Reed, the versatility that he could play safety and corner, was that something you all identified with him back even at you South Dakota or was that something that he did [clears throat] starting here? >> I would say for him, he played more cornerback, nickel. Uh, that's just That's just what comes up with injuries. That happens year-round, unfortunately, with football. Yeah, certainly we had, you know, a number of them going into this these roster decisions this weekend, but I think we're doing a good job managing it, balancing, you know, giving ourselves as many opportunities as we can with these guys. Understand where, you know, a couple guys go to IR and we're going to lose them for an extended period of time, but we'll be we'll be all right. >> As of right now, are you anticipating anybody else going on IR besides those two? >> Uh, potentially potentially a couple in just in the next few days. But um yeah, he's a great kid. >> Uh how much like have you guys been been already getting the game plan ready for Detroit at this stage or are you kind of just like turning more of your attention toward that now that your roster evaluation >> Yeah, we're turning there. And now it's just honing in on the details, the fundamentals, all that sort of stuff. Uh, cuz he's going to have a really good career in this league, and he's going to be a really good player, and you know, it's going to come down to the consistency of all the technique and fundamentals. And so, I think the good benefit for him is he's in a really good room to learn and grow from. Just uh, you know, best for best for the the team and just the roster management and you know, obviously we we had to keep you know, you're only going to be able to keep 53 guys, and so sometimes you're going to have to make tough decisions, and um, hope that they can still be a part of your team in some capacity, and sometimes it doesn't work out that way. You guys got the >> [laughter] >> I'll leave the same all. >> Zamir White, you know, was it kind of a emphasis to kind of get him involved so that you could potentially keep him around? Those three earned it. Not every team carries three on the active roster and all three of those guys earned the opportunity to be on the 53. They're We got three really good QBs. >> On the announcer here, Samir White is included on the practice squad.
