title: Saints OG Jeremiah Wright on his love for the game and bringing energy to the field
text: It seemed like there was a because you had the penalty against the Rams and it seemed like there was a similar situation. You kind of kind of pulled up against the against the Cowboys that like I definitely did. I kind of seen kind of like a flashback. I seen the exact thing happening. So I was like running. I like ready to ease up. I like no won't get me again. So but just a learning learning thing. Just get better each and every day. The >> coaches give you a hard time. >> No, just play ball. Still be me. >> Yeah. I mean, and it has to be a balance, right? Because you want to, like you said, control the direction, but also you don't want to lose kind of what makes you >> special as a as a player and that physicality. Like, how do you balance that? >> Um, it kind of hard for me cuz I mean like that's Jay, right? Go out there loud, physical, show emotion. Um, so I kind of just tell myself in my mind, make a big play, big block, control it, celebrate my mind or whatever, but control it. And we get in the end zone now. I can do whatever long as I don't get no fine. Don't do nothing crazy, but I can do whatever I want to with the team to celebrate with the team. >> When you first got here, we talked about the learning curve and playing in the SEC. How much have you leaned on maybe playing in the SEC or has it been a little more different than you thought now after having all this offseason work? >> Um, kind of I wouldn't say not too different, not too far off cuz like I say, all the guys that make it to, you know, this level, they're blessed. They're great guys. No matter what school, college they played for, they're all great players. So, I mean, it really don't don't mean that. We all still here together to grow and learn from each other. And lastly, just what's your excitement level for this team now that we are inching closer to a regular season? >> I'm ready. I'm ready to go. Ready to see, you know, this team make some noise and go out here and win some games. And >> just one more question. You know, a player that people don't know a ton about is Will Sherman. You got to play with him a lot during the preseason. What have you seen from Will? >> Oh, yeah. That's another guy that I kind of leaned on from his, you know, Wilson of the game. Um, just him being here, it's like, man, him coming in helping me. Well, me coming in, him helping me, it was like I say like night and day from the first day I got here to like now he's like, "Man, you really grown and know kind of a great player." So, I just keep learning from him each and every day. >> Is it kind of crazy to see a guy that can play like to all five spots if he needed him to? That's got to be kind of cool. >> Like I used to watch uh some of his old games and then I see him slide out the tackle then he be at guard and be like, "Man, you you athletic out there moving." He's like, "Oh yeah, JR, I do it all." So, kind of see a guy like that that can do all five. Definitely a guy you can learn from, you know, he's very smart, intelligent player. >> You go one second. >> Where do you feel like you made the most growth like throughout camp from the time you got here until right now standing here? >> Yeah. Um, like I said earlier, just the fundamentals and technique part, the different things that my coach and players teach me in the past game. Um, that's kind of like my biggest growth. just seeing how I was and the different things and techniques that I was taught in college and getting here and you know elevating my game is kind of like night and day. >> And just what's the goal for you now now that you're you're on the 53 and you know you made the team like where are you trying to to grow now to to just you know earn reps and you know get get some more opportunity? >> Yeah, just take it day by day. Don't look you know ahead of the next day. Just take it day by day. Learn from the vets and just keep being Jay right. Is that ever hard to do to just kind of stay in the moment and like not like look big picture, you know? >> Um, no. Cuz I mean I've been doing this since I was little. I didn't start playing football till I was in the sixth grade. So, um, kind of was never looking forward to the big game. We always been taught every coach that I had just take it day by day. and don't look for the next week cuz you know you seen it happen in college plenty of times where guys be focused on the next week game and the game coming up they end up taking a loss and you know too focused on whatever big game that's coming up next. So let's take it day by day. >> Where do you feel like your love of the game comes from? Um, I'll just say just watching my mom and grandma growing up, uh, just seeing how hard they work and I was like, man, it's like they're like, Jay, right? How, you know, you see me now, you see how I am kind of true, cool, jolly player, but then it's like I get on the fields like a whole different person. I think I kind of get that from mom and grandmama. So, I just flip a switch like soon I put the helmet on and I step foot on the field, it's it's go mode. What did they do growing up? Like where' they work? >> Um my grandma, she worked at uh job called herillyw. They like worked on cars and everything. Um mom, my grandma pretty much she did a lot of cooking and everything. So I used to watch Granny cook, still do watch her cook. Uh trying to get some her recipe, trying to get her to make me a book. Um yeah, and then mom's pretty much the same. Yeah. So is it kind of like respecting the opportunity you you have to like you know after seeing how hard they work like you get a chance to do this kind of comes from >> most definitely. >> Yeah. And um how you feel like that that just helps you grow in the game like you love what you do you love the opportunity like do you feel like that helps you like learn fast develop fast like how how does that kind of show? >> Yeah definitely do. um just being there with mom and grandma and my two sisters and with me have to be take on that male role early in life. It's like, you know, I was just ready to go and just ready to help my family grow, too. Also, not just on the field, off the field, too. Building, you know, our relationships cuz it's kind of hard when you're away from family. You ain't talking to them as much as you were when you was growing up. So, kind of trying to, you know, get better at balancing life with, you know, NFL football and going from there. and just kind of like out on the field like you know I mentioned this to you the other day like you know the belt to ass and just kind of how you're getting like you know people fired up like >> where's that like you you just kind of like being the guy out there >> yeah I just I come up with all type of celebrations and different things um that was one first down celebration that's another one that was a big one kind of like the first one I pulled out first day got here first down celebration then went to the belt so >> I'll come up with some different ones on during the season, you know.

title: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. on not playing in preseason and building chemistry with the O-Line
text: Not having this preseason. This is my first time not playing in a preseason. I mean kind of feel like it was weird but it it was well deserved and I feel like coach has a plan for us. He knows that he wants us to be our best when it's week 17 going into the playoffs. And that's what we looking forward to. >> What's your vision for how explosive this offense can be now? >> I mean the sky's the limit. We just got to continue to just focus on the little details. I feel like the minute details, the things that's going to help us just be explosive. But first we got to focus on not having penalties, not having offsides, not having false starts and things like that. And just try to matriculate the ball down field, take what the defense gives us. And that's when you're going to see explosive happens whenever we just fall in love with the mundane and just keep moving the ball. Then those explosives going to come. >> You mentioned being healthy going to the regular season. How important I guess is it for you to be available because you know because of the depth? >> I mean I mean it's very important to me. Uh I've been out for a year. I had a Lisfranc so just being away from the game and just understanding that that health is wealth, you know, and that they pay me to be here because I'm consistent and I'm available each and every Sunday. So I just got to continue to maintain and take care of my body. So whenever my name is called, my number called, I'm ready. >> Did that injury change the way you feel about getting ready in the preseason at all? Like >> No cuz that injury happened in the preseason game. It was my rookie year and I played every preseason after that but this one, you know. And I mean I was more than ready to play. But coach had you know, he's looking out for our future. He has the best interest in us as a team and as a and as a whole. So uh you got to continue to keep working. >> And how did it feel just putting on the Saints uniform, going through warm-ups and Dallas and just getting, you know, a taste of at least the uniform with that? >> Man, it felt like it felt like somebody like put a cake in front of my face and told me I can't eat it, you know. So it was just it was it was great but it was kind of different experience, you know, once you get out there give it to the guys. You feeling the energy. You just ready to play, you know. But our is like, "Nah, I'm going to take the pads off." And you're kind of like, "Damn, back to this." But uh we'll be there real soon, you know, so I feel like uh I have I have my time to show the world what I can do. >> Up to that point, what did it feel like not playing in the preseason in a different situation like you earned that opportunity? >> Yeah, now I feel weird cuz I feel like all right, usually like the guys like like AK now they play preseason like the superstar and stuff like that and like just kind of uh be receiving that treatment is kind of crazy uh because I'm just used to playing like all right. It's like a mindset, I guess, but just uh understanding that coach has our best interest for our team, our depth, and the things that we want for the future. Um I'm just blessed to be here, honestly. >> Did you say matriculate the ball down the field? Do you know anything about Hank Stram? >> Who? >> Hank Stram. >> [laughter] >> Now I know Drew Brees is just taking his deep and digging digging dive and just get them just move the ball down the field and whenever the defense kind of comes up, take that take that uh deep shot down the field. So uh and then Tom Brady just the greatest you see all the greatest taking deep shots gives him the kind of play chess uh and that's that's when you have a great team. >> Yeah, that was something something Hank Stram said long before you were born, probably. >> Now I appreciate the >> my question. I mean, when you watch the success that everyone was able to have in that game, how excited does that make you about this run game in general cuz it's not just one guy, it's the entire group? >> Now I mean, it's very exciting, honestly, but uh I've I've I've been in the league long enough to know, man, preseason is preseason. I think uh my first year we went 3 and 0 in preseason and won game in the the rest of the year. So you try to not get too high, but you have hope for the future and uh we're coming out versus a tough opponent Detroit Lions, so I'm pretty sure they're going to be ready to stop the run, so we just got to go put that on film week one, you know, and then keep doing it consistently and then we'll talk about how great the run game was after the season. >> How do you feel like you kind of developed all through through camp? I mean, I know you weren't here last year, but like it feels like, you know, watching it that there's a pretty good, you know, something coming together right now in the in the run game. >> Oh, you know, for sure. I feel like uh just through camp you just kind of get a feel for my I got a I got a feel for my offensive line. Just continue to stand what they want to do and how they like to move people or how they're looking at people setting leverages up and just kind of getting a feel for them and I feel like uh, we're going to continue to just get better because the more reps we get together, uh, we're just going to kind of just get in sync and just know what each other's going to do. >> Is there chemistry there between you and the offensive line? Like you you learn how they move and that allows you to kind of like set up your cuts and stuff like that? >> No, for sure, man. I I've been playing running back with my whole life, so uh, I feel like being in sync, uh, is the best thing you can do with your offensive line. Uh, I truly believe that a running back is a byproduct of his offensive line, you know, like if if they don't get things moving for me, uh, nothing will happen, you know, so uh, all credit goes to them, you know, each and every game, so uh, whenever they're at their best, I'm at my best. And uh, whenever something happens, then I got to make something miss, but I feel like we're building that chemistry to where we know what each other's thinking and uh, we know that we're trying to just move the ball down the field every time. >> So, like are you like reading like David Edwards' body language and kind of taking like mental notes as you're going through reps so you know what's going to happen next time or which way he might be moving like that? That's kind of how that works? >> Yeah, no, that that that's definitely how it works. Just like just understanding it first it it starts with understanding the the scheme, understanding where he's going and then like you say, like just from time on time you start understanding his leverage, start seeing where he want to take the defenders and feel like for David it's it's it's easy for him. He just moves them out the way, so uh, just just be patient, get behind uh, David and he he he'll get the job done. >> That's a big ass dude. >> No, for sure. >> No, I feel like all the offensive line is is is is real big, man. That's what you want and uh, for it really got me excited for the season. >> So, like if if there's a new guy coming in, like are you studying them? Like the the line like you putting on his film and like watching them and kind of trying to pick some stuff up or is that or is that just out on the field really? >> No, no, not really. Not putting on his film and studying them. Now, you said I might go study them now, but uh, it's more so just time on time. I feel like that's why we go through camp. That's why we go through OTAs so we get that feel. I mean, uh, you don't get no better experience than repetition. And uh just understanding and just getting that that flow state with the offensive line. Uh that comes from just reps, reps, reps. And uh that's what we've been doing out here. >> I was looking at it like a lot of guys like their inside zone runner, outside zone runner numbers will be a little bit better than one of the other. Like you're even kind of across the board. Like do you do you have a preference or you just you just hitting it? >> You know, man, I'm just trying to like like I'm just trying to do what the team needs, you know? I feel like to be a great running back you got to be able to do every everything. You can't just be a outside zone runner. You can't really just be a inside zone runner, man. The league is too good. They got too many good defensive coordinators. There's too many people that can just shut one thing down, you know? So, you have to find a way to continue to move the ball down the field. And at the end of the day, it's all about playing football more so. And I feel like it it really becomes more situational than um inside zone, outside zone. Cuz if it's third and one, my my job is to get the first down. No one cares if it's outside or inside zone. Long as I get that one yard, we just keep moving the ball down field. So, uh we just keep it football and just understand that we get just how confident we are paid to be here. And I just do what I've always been doing. Uh things things work out well.

Um his ability to block at the point of attack has been um has been really really good. And then his ability to make plays in the red zone has been good to him. title: Bucs 53-Man Roster Reaction Show | Training Camp Report | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Welcome into our final training camp report presented by Advent. Casey Phillips here with senior writer and editor Scott Smith. And of course, this is a bit of a different way to do a training camp report. This is the final 53man roster, which we say final. >> It's it's kind of the >> forever fluid. >> It's kind of the culmination of everything that happened. >> That's right. >> Where we were trying to get to. >> Based on training camp, we now have our 53 and man roster, which again, we always like to give the asterisk. It can always be changing. It's always Yes, it is inevitable. But as of the cutdowns that are required to happen at a certain point, we wanted to go over the the final 53 and some of the interesting notes that have come from it. And of course, I feel like we have to start with the quarterback situation. That's been already one of the really interesting storylines of camp and it culminated in an interesting note of the 53. >> I mean, I think we saw the writing on the wall that Jaylen Daniels was going to make this team when he played the majority of the game on Friday night in Jacksonville. Uh he had a very nice preseason. Of course, it nothing much went right in offense in the last game, but he did lead five scoring drives. Uh I guess in the other two games, I guess the uh bigger part of that story was wasn't clear if the Bucks were going to keep two or three. And the answer is two because they they let go of both Jake Browning and Connor Baslack. There will of course be a third quarterback on the practice squad. It could be one of those two guys. It could be somebody else, but uh Jaylen Daniels is the primary backup to Baker Mayfield. You know, and one of the things we always talk about with the 53 is when you keep either more or less at any given position group, that ends up giving you or removing a spot somewhere else. And so, um, based on the fact that, you know, you only have two quarterbacks that's going to affect some things on offense, but also, of course, on defense, are there certain position groups on either side of the ball that stood out to you as having either more or less than you expected? >> Seven defensive linemen. And we talked all through camp about how deep that spot was and how it was going to be hard that there were eight or nine guys that you could reasonably see making the roster. ends up being seven um including the rookie Damonte Kart. Uh so and I I was going to mention later, but I might as well mention now all seven draft picks from this year made the team >> which is very cool. Um I know that there were a couple cuts from another draft class though as to kind of you know counteract that. >> Well, you know there's turnover and and we've got we have 10 new rookies and and some additions in free agency and sometimes that means players that were on this roster the last few years their spots are beaten out by somebody else. So, three members of the 24 draft class, edge rusher Chris Brazwell, uh, tight end Devin Culp, and guard Elijah Klein were all among the cuts today. >> And then, I know we always like talking about every year undrafted free agents, there's going to be a few that make it, and of course, we already mentioned Jaylen Daniels being one of those, but who else from the undrafted group was able to make that 53? >> Every year. Every year, you can count on it. And I don't think any of them were surprises based on their play in preseason and training camp. We already talked about Jaylen Daniels. Also, cornerback Aiden Garn, one of the biggest stories of camp in the preseason. Just kept making plays in every practice in every game. And and you know, there's not a lot of, you know, there's a need for quarterback dub. This is a guy if we run into any injuries has a chance, a real chance to play. And then, um, Kaden Forom, and this was one that I was actually talking about the other day. I feel like I kind of made a good prediction there that Kaden Forom basically leaprogged over last year's undrafted linebackers, John Bullock and Nick Jackson. He got the last linebacker spot and those other two were waved. And um it's not just that he played well on defense, which he did, but that guy, did you notice he had three special teams tackles on Friday night? Amazing. >> If you're trying to win the last spot on a roster and you have three special teams tackles, that's the way to do it. >> Yeah, absolutely. >> Good for him finishing up strong. >> Good for him. Absolutely. So those were some of our kind of highlevel storylines from the 53, but wanted to go position by position just to make sure everyone sees kind of the the full roster and how it shaked out by group. So of course we did already kind of talk about the quarterbacks, that's an easy one, two, you know who they are. So yes, those those are your two. Uh so wide receiver, I always think this is an interesting one of especially based on how many quarterbacks you keep and you know just all the different position groups between tight end, running back, and wide receiver. How do you allocate those last spots? So, what was what kind of stood out to you about who they kept and how many? >> And if you had a guy that's not on this list here that you really liked, um there's a good chance they'll be back on the practice squad. So, don't write them off. And if you're on the practice squad, you're probably going to play at some point during the season, but kept six, which is a pretty standard number. Last year, however, we kept seven because Chris Godwin wasn't ready to go. And I think it's worth noting that um we had 27 players waved, including three who were waved with an injury designation. two guys, um Josh Hayes and David Sills put on injur reserve and they can those are your two options to do that. They can actually come back after four games and then um three uh veterans that were terminated and uh we didn't put anybody on a reserve pup or reserve NFI list and that's good news. I know we're all waiting with baited breath for Jayla McMillan and Amecha Ibuka to get back in the mix but they're not on any kind of list and I think that's very good news. >> That is very good news. And then all right so now moving on to running backs. This was another one that there was some question about that RB3 position. Do they keep three? Do they keep four? Who would be number three? So, where did that end up? >> I'm glad I didn't have to go on the record for that because I would have I would have predicted that we'd keep four. But, uh, and it looked like if they weren't going to keep four, obviously pretty Kenny Gable and Bucky Irving are your year 1 A and 1B. But, um, would Sean Tucker hold off the, uh, challenge from Josh Williams, a first year player because he spent most of last year, uh, on injur. So, I guess that makes him a second year player. um he made the roster out of camp last year but then was hurt for much of the season. So he seemed to be a real threat but he was not. So we have three >> three running backs. Yep. All right. So then now tight end. This is another one where um we mentioned the the draft pick thing over the last few years of who got kept and who did not. So uh this is a group that hadn't had turnover at all in years and and finally there is one spot that has changed hands. We could have gone in with the same group, but it seemed pretty obvious as training camp and the preseason progressed that you had your three of Kat and Payne Durham and um Kokeeft, but that it was probably going to be a battle between incumbent Devin Culp and the rookie Bower Sharp. And as we see, they chose to keep Bower Sharp. And I think you could see that in in the results of the game. He I think he played a lot more than Deon and he certainly had more production. >> Yeah. And I think his special teams contributions >> Yeah, he did well, too. That's a great point. >> Yep. So, all right. Now, uh, offensive line, you saw this was a group that boy was depth important last year. And so, uh, what did that tell you about a who they kept, how many they kept, and what those backups could look like after seeing a lot of them in the preseason? >> Went with 10, which is which is usually the highest number you go with on offensive line, at least to start the season, because that means you kept your five stars and five backups. Um, and probably only eight of those 10 are going to be active on game day. So, keeping we we could talk about the starters. Everybody knows that five and we're excited about it. But keeping all three of Dan Feny, Luke Haggard, and rookie Billy Shrath for the interior and then both Justin School and Ben Chukuma as tackles. I think that says something to um there there's a couple guys that are banged up like Chuck Wuma and Shrath, but also they really like those guys, you know, they like Shout, they like Chuck Wuma, and uh these are they resigned Dan Feny in the offseason. So, these are deaf players that they didn't want to lose. >> Um, all right. Now, moving on to the defensive side of things. Uh, defensive linemen, we kind of hit on this earlier that uh we we kept we kept a lot of them. Uh, so tell me your your main thoughts on the defensive line that we were able to build. >> I I think you're going to see maybe you'd probably keep six of those active on game day. Sometimes maybe five, but seven. There's going to be a lot of um rotation and you got a you got a good mix of different types of players. We know what Vita is. Ky's more that win uh you know at the line of scrimmage and get pressure up the middle kind of guy. Um you got Rake Nunes Roaches and and Aan Robinson to help you set that tone uh more nasty tone up front. Elijah Roberts got to play a lot last year. So it's a really good group and I also like the diversity of it. >> Yeah, I agree with that. All right, so outside linebacker, uh this was a group that I I thought was going to be an interesting one, especially knowing that, you know, a guy like Jack Pyurn had gotten a lot of attention. Uh, so tell me about how many they kept and and what stands out to you. >> I would imagine I would have to imagine the Jack Pyram was one of the tougher decisions when you're getting down to the end there and you're trying to figure out how to get to 53. Um, kept five and four of those will probably you usually have a fourman rotation. Um, but I could see all five of these being active on game day because if you I don't know if you say Anthony Nelson is your fifth pass rusher. Well, he just did really well in the preseason and also he just always kills it on special teams. So, I think you'd want him active for that. So, this is the group of course that we are so excited about being um uh much more productive this year with the additions of Ruben Bane and Alcadine Muhammad and David Walker coming back from IR. >> Yeah, that's going to be a fun group to watch. Uh for sure. All right, inside linebacker. Um this has been interesting from a both starting standpoint with, you know, bringing in somebody like a Josiah Troder to challenge for that starting role and then also just depth. But then there were injuries that have made it kind of hard to assess that group. >> Yeah. But two of the guys that have been dealing with injuries, Cervasio Dennis and and Christian Rosenbone did both make the team. So I think that's an indication that they're probably pretty close to coming back. Um if you if you want to predict as I probably would that Josiah Troder the rookie is going to win that other starting spot. It has not been announced but that's a prediction next to Analone. I think you can see how the other three Dennis and Forom and Roseboom are all going to be key special teams players and depth of course if we need >> for sure. Yes. >> Somebody to fill in. So corner and we can maybe kind of combine this of of corner and safety. There's DB's overall is is a position that looks a little light when you look at the numbers. >> It's only eight at the moment. Five corners and that's it says five corners and three safeties but remember Keiant Scott can play both. So it's really more like >> almost >> it's almost even. Um but that's still overall light. eight defensive backs. And that's where I would suggest you're probably, you know, you tend to see a few moves once everybody around the league makes their cuts and you get a good look at guys you might like who are suddenly available because eight is really light to go at DB. And I wouldn't be surprised if there are some moves coming in the next week. >> That makes a lot of sense. All right. So then finally, of course, the specialists, which we can just copy paste, all the same guys from last year. They're back. >> Long snacker sap snapper Evan Deckers. >> Long snapper Evan Deckers. >> That's funny. I've never realized that that's kind of >> Sally sells seashells. >> Uh he did hold off in a challenge from veteran Scott Daly who they both snapped in each game so that was definitely a competition and I don't think there was much of a real competition between BT Potter or Chase Mclofflin. But BT Potter got a chance to put some more on tape so maybe he can find a spot somewhere in the league. >> Yep. All right. Well, that is going to do it for us right now on this full 53man roster. Again, there are inevitably always a few changes after this happens and of course the practice squad still yet to be named. So stay tuned for both of those moves and coverages coming up over these next few days.

title: Malik Nabers: 'The main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can' | New York Giants
text: What was the feeling in the in the room and the locker room and the receiver room when you guys found out that Odell made this team? >> Um, you know, he's he's put in great work. Um, he showed, you know, every attribute and everything that he wanted to be a giant. He wanted to be here. he wanted to, you know, come back and, you know, he had unfinished business and we talked all the time, you know, through the offseason and, you know, summer about things that he wanted to accomplish and this was one of the main things was coming back, um, making the team and, you know, they didn't make it easy for him. You know, he earned everything he got. Um, you know, he put great film on tape. I'm sure everybody seen. Um, he was a great leader. So, you know, good things get rewarded to good people, you know, for sure. And then, like I said, he's been a great leader. So, you know, to have him in there is, you know, it's definitely a good good choice. >> What's he mean to you just specifically over this camp? What's it been like to have him to rely on it [clears throat] and turn to? >> Yeah, I mean, he's come up, you know, many times and just, you know, ask me about the rehab process, you know, try to give me, you know, tips and things to do that helped him, you know, during his rehab. Um, and, you know, asking me continue to ask what I'm doing, you know, telling me I can do more. You can do more. Um, you know, he wanted to see me back out there. He's excited, you know, to see me run routes and, you know, I'm excited to, you know, also, you know, be on side of him playing. Um, you know, I used to watch him when I was younger, so just to be here right now is it's probably it's crazy, you know, as it seems. But, um, you know, like I say, he's been a great leader for sure. >> Did you watch his one-handed catch live on TV when it happened? >> No, no, no. I I was I wasn't really a uh football fan when I was growing up. like he kind of like he kind of was the base person that literally like made me start watching, you know, football. Um, you know, just, you know, the dances, the one-handers, and, you know, he he was probably was the first person I started really watching, you know, when I started playing football. Um, he was, you know, the main person. So, just for him being here right now, you know, in the same room as me, it's it's it's so real. You know, sometimes I got to, you know, take a moment. Um, but, you know, just have him here is is actually amazing. you know what you thought about him as a player before he got here and then >> we know last year social media you guys got involved you know come here come here let's finish it >> how different is the Odell that you knew from afar to the Odell that you've seen the last two months here >> I mean [clears throat] he's seen a lot I mean you can tell just his you know demeanor is different um everything that he does is is just different you know he has his you know he has his things that he he goes through the weekly just keeping his body healthy um you showing great, you know, great, you know, charisma just being out here. Um, he wants to be here. Um, he feels like he has, you know, unfinished business and he's carrying that, you know, every day at practice. You see him come out here. He's always, you know, um, before pre-practice, he's running fast. He's always doing extra more um catching jugs. So, he wants he wants to be here and he wants to um continue to, you know, build his legacy. So just seeing, you know, how he's turned over from the last two years of him, you know, probably being in the darkest, you know, room that he's probably been in and to come out of there, you know, and still have that same demeanor that we all seen in him when he was here. Um, that great, you know, great character and just, you know, coming out here and trying to outwork somebody. So just to keep having that and carry on to that, you know, it's been amazing to watch him. >> How are you feeling and what checkpoints remain between now and the opener for you to get through? Um, I mean, I'm going to keep the checkpoints in house. Um, really it's not it's not really really anything too big, but like I said, I'm going to keep it more in house and just, you know, to myself. >> Well, how are you feeling then, I guess? >> Uh, I feel pretty good. Um, well, I feel real good to be honest. Um, but, you know, like I said, you know, you gonna feel good, but there still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to, you know, participate. So I'm still, you know, going through that. Still listening to the trainers, still listening to, you know, doctors and, you know, sharing everything with them. >> Training camp's done now, right? You is your mind [clears throat] focused fully on playing against the Cowboys now at this point? >> Uh, my mind is focused on playing, you know, the regular season, playing whenever that is and playing what team it is. you know, I'm going to be making sure that I'm ready to go out there and, you know, and I'm healthy enough to, you know, play all four quarters that, you know, nobody got to, you know, make sure, you know, I'm not in on every play or they have to make sure I got enough snaps to play all, you know, my snaps are limited. So, that's the main focus is just trying to be out there as much as I can. >> At this point though, from our perspective, we're like looking at [clears throat] you and we're like, well, why wouldn't he play? >> What would you say to that? Like, is there anything that is there any reason you wouldn't be able to play at this point? like if the Super Bowl was tomorrow, would you be able to get on the field and play? >> Um, that'll be a decision that, you know, that would be made, you know, when that time comes. Um, like I say, you know, the outside view, you know, I might look like, you know, I'm 100%. I make I make everything look well. I mean, you know, sometimes I run routes and I go look on the internet and I'm like, dang, I was moving kind of crazy. But, you know, when you're in your body and you're in it, you know, you still have some things that you still got to work on as, you know, a football player that you got to be like, you know, I'm not I don't feel right doing this cut. I don't feel right. I haven't been hit. I haven't seen this. So, it's certain things that you just got to, as a football player, you got to mentally prepare that before you go into a game. Regarding his contract, in your opinion, why is it deal not gotten done with him? I what I what I I really like is the fact that just I've watched these guys from the spring to where they are now and how they've grown. So, >> well, when you have two guys that were high draft picks like Broadick and Kale Johnson that don't pan out here, what lessons can you learn from that or what can you take to ensure that something like that doesn't happen going forward? >> Yeah, the I'll just say those guys, you know, I I um I think both those guys still have a lot of football good football in them and I think they're only going to get better and you know, in those situations, every one of these situations a little different, but uh a change of scenery is just might be, you know, could be good for everyone. >> One more when you keep so many choices like you have and then you have to move on from number one picks with number three picks. How how do you balance that? Uh, you know, just in your own feelings when you evaluate everything. >> Yeah, you know, you Jerry, the way I I always look at it is it's important when you draft a player to to get them to that next contract, you know, and obviously when when they don't make it to that second contract or third contract, that's disappointing. And in this situation, you know, with Brick and Caleb, we didn't get there. And u that's on me. But uh like I said, I I I still think those guys have good football. >> I think Broadick uh Red shirt sophomore had like 17 games starting experience in college. Since then, Troy had a ton of experience. Derek as well, and I think Max Max had a decent amount, too. Did you change your philosophy at all with, you know, going after older players who maybe had more experience um after drafting Carter? No, I I wouldn't say we changed the philosophy, but I think, you know, when you go through the process and experience helps, you know, in different situations, uh, require you to maybe look at guys who who've played more than others and, you know, you weigh every situation differently. >> Amar, did Sean report anything to you guys after that game against the Jets that raised any concern? No, we I mean we saw how how maybe his uh his knee or his body responded to it and u not necessarily a setback, but it was good for us to go through and um it's a long season and um we just felt like you know what, the right thing to do is he he had a significant injury, right? So, it was just let's just be smart about it. Let's not rush anything. Make sure we're all we're all um we're all comfortable with everything. So, let's just um you know, and he's you guys know him, he's a warrior. I mean, I mean, he if he walked in here and I said, "Hey, give me a thousand push-ups." He's gonna give us 2,000 right there. So, uh, he's, uh, so it just it was the right thing to do. >> You cut a couple veteran Dlinemen and kept droy. What did he show you? >> He earned it, man. I got to give him credit. title: REACTING to the Pittsburgh Steelers' 53-man roster
text: Back to Steelers Breakdown. Nick Farbar here with you guys. A Sunday episode kind of out of the blue, but I think very much a worthy one when you think about the Cutdown Day happening and the Pittsburgh Steelers now at 53 players. Some surprises. Um seemingly going to be naturally some movement coming here uh into the future because the Steelers certainly need it. Um, with safety being thin, um, I think there are a few show a few uh, positions that you look at and you say, "Man, that is pretty thin." And safety's the big one. Um, we also can talk about inside linebacker, I think, being one. But some surprising moves, and I guess let's start with just the surprises. I'm not sure any of us really thought Kevin Joy Jr. was going to make this roster. That one I think is a pretty big surprise. I I think we can look at that one and I don't know how many 53man roster projections around the league and really around the local media had him on their 53man roster. Um and and rightfully so. He was pretty quiet most of the of the summer. He didn't really get a ton of run. Um, and so that to me, um, is a surprise, but he's got good traits. Atlanta Roberts getting cut out of that inside linebacker room. I think a lot of us had five projected. I think naturally E- Rob had a great training camp. I think he had a great two preseason games he played in. Looked like the run stuffer he's always been, but gets chopped. Um, not a lot of special teams there. I get it. But I still think a very worthy player. Um, you know, I I think you look at some of the moves they made in at safety. Um, Desawn Elliott to IR. Um, I think that is a huge one. Maybe the biggest thing to take away from this was seeing Deshawn go to injured reserve. Um, Joey Porter Jr. being activated from the pup. So, that's the latest in that saga. So much to break down, but let's talk about this. So quarterback, obviously they naturally keep four quarterbacks um on their roster. We had talked about this dating back to Lord probably the draft um as that could they keep four quarterbacks after they took Drew Aller. It made a good deal of sense at least that they would. I I don't necessarily agree with the roster building strategy. I think that you look at it, it's going to be tough with flexibility, especially if you're calling uh players up just to do it. Um, but the Pittsburgh Steelers certainly could look uh to try and maximize that and they can kind of move and play roster musical chairs if they they will. Um, clearly this is trying to play the both sides game, right? trying to get the guys that they feel are best now, Aaron Rogers. And if Rogers gets nicked for a game or two, Mason Rudolph, and then if you have this future, you want to develop both Will Howard and Drew Aller, it's fairly clear they're trying to play both sides of this coin. And so this four quarterback idea, it's going to hurt them roster flexibility-wise. Remember, only three practice squad elevations for a one player. So at some point, those players that keep getting elevated have to be added to the 53. They can wheel and deal, but it might leave them short somewhere else on their roster. Only three quarterbacks can really be active. That third quarterback has designations on his roster participation, but one of those quarterbacks, probably Drew Aller, I would guess, is naturally going to be uh inactive and straight up inactive for most of these games. So, it's interesting. They are not the only team to do that this year. I think there's three other teams that also kept four quarterbacks. Um, so that's kind of an interesting trend. It seems like the Steelers were actually in line with the league trend that a lot of these teams were keeping four quarterbacks at running back. This was one of those that I think was a little surprising. Not as much after what we saw Thursday. Eli Hidenrike beats out Travis Homer, Lou Nichols, Caleb Johnson. Caleb Johnson got traded. Um, to me, Eli Hidenrike did a pretty good job stamping his case that day. I think he looked like a real NFL football player for really the first time in a long time. Um, and I think that partially was due to the position switch. He wasn't really a true running back at Navy. He was more of a he was what they call a snipe. So, he played more like slot receiver um at Navy. And so, they made him a running back here. I thought his pass reps were very encouraging. We saw him make a special teams tackle. He was the personal protector. He ran with really good force behind his pads. We know he can catch out of the back field. There's a lot of utility with Eli Heinrike. And I think with the way he took the tough parts of the position, running between the tackles, running with physicality, the pass pro, you know, you have special teams versatility. He could be a returner alongside Kaden, there's so much utility in the type of player he is. He can condense so many roles and and so I'm not surprised he made the 53. And I think actually, you know, there's a real argument for that. Now, Lou Nichols, I think, had a phenomenal preseason. I think is the third true running back in terms of skill. Um, and maybe we even see Travis Homer come up a little bit from the practice squad. Certainly, I think he's a practice squad candidate and could be added. I think Lou Nichols is another practice squad candidate they would really like to have. Um, but I do think, you know, if there were an injury, let's say Rico Data or Jaylen Warren got hurt, they would probably elevate Lou Nichols to actually play running back. But I think they feel that, you know, Eli Henrik can be a guy that fills in. And so, good for Eli Hidenrike. I think he put a good case up in that Buffalo game. Not a surprise to me. I think there's a lot more to his game that we haven't seen. Um, Caleb Johnson, let's talk about this. So, they trade Caleb Johnson. Um, this one to me was not a surprise at all. We had talked about how he fell out of favor. It seemed like in the summer he started out training camp as the running back three, and it certainly seemed like at that point we were going to see KJ make this roster. Um, and then it just came kind of crashing down once the pads came on. He started running with like a fifth, you know, the third, fourth strings. Um, you not getting second and first team reps that he wasn't even getting the types of reps that Travis Homer and Lou Nichols were in the preseason. text: The 49ers 53-man roster, it is not a complete structure like Coit Tower behind me. It is much more like an evolving skyline. Telegraph Hill is the spot for the big 53-man roster show this year. A peaceful Sunday afternoon and we look through the initial 49ers build because this is going to change as soon as today. In fact, we can start with the linebacker position where the 49ers took seven. Fred Warner, Dre Greenlaw, Jaden Dogger, Garrett Wallo. We were certain about all those guys. Tayden Bathen has made the team for the 49ers as well, but both Nick Martin and Luke Gifford made the 53 with hamstring injuries. And this is where you have to get smart when you're looking at the 53-man roster construction because today, I can almost guarantee you that at least one of those two, maybe both of Martin and Luke Gifford will be placed on injured reserve. And the reason for that is you have to make the initial 53-man roster to be eligible to return from injured reserve. Your season is done. Like Brett Toth's season, like Nick Zakelj's season. Your season is done if you go on IR before making the 53. So, what the 49ers are doing here is creative, but not unprecedented. Seven linebackers, moves coming, and then we'll see will Larry Worth with his long frame make that practice squad. I think the 49ers certainly would like for that to happen. title: Notre Dame HC Marcus Freeman Talks CFP Snub, CJ Carr & More I Full Interview I The Rich Eisen Show
text: Being a Michigan guy, I I'm I'm I'm supposed to not like this man, but he's too damn likable. >> [laughter] >> And his quarterback is Lloyd's grandson. My goodness gracious. Marcus Freeman of Notre Dame football back on the program. How are you, coach? >> How are you, Rick? >> And you played for Ohio State. I'm supposed to not like you like every fiber of your being I'm supposed to not like, but you're so likable, man. >> We can overcome that. >> You know, is that is I need to have a better growth mindset is basically >> That's it. >> You you're you're coaching me up right now I have a feeling. You know, that's pretty cool. So, you were you were you were on the BCS championship team >> twice >> twice with with Ohio State, right? >> Yep. Lost to Florida coached by Urban Meyer and that was Tim Tebow's freshman year and the next year we lost to LSU. >> Damn. And that was Tressel, right? Tressel was your coach? >> That's right. >> What was he like as a coach? >> Unbelievable. Um I you know, I think you sometimes take for granted the leadership that he displayed as a player. Um just you just thought it was normal and as I get older and reflect, he is uh so unique in his leadership style and his ability to put the the interest of and the needs of the people he's leading in front of himself. And um he still teaches me that here at 40 years old. I was with him at a football game. Actually, Ted Ginn who was the head coach of the Aviators, um we went to go watch him and uh I took two of my boys with me and he takes us to a suite, tells us to sit down, next thing I know 2 minutes later he's passing out waters to his former player to his former player's kids. Um then he comes around with a a a of cookies and I just remember going he's still serving his players. It should be the other way around. And uh he's unbelievable, man. >> Well, I mean, now you're you're in a college football world where, you know, somebody having to account for tattoos, you know, would be You know what I mean? Like it's insane what happened compared to what's going on in college football right now. Does that ever hit you? Does that ever land on you at any moment in time? >> Yeah, I mean, I don't Sometimes I I I think back to it in in you know, the biggest thing is I know is Jim Tressel's a great person. >> Right. >> And for him to maybe be portrayed in a way that wasn't a good person and and to to lose his job is the things that I know Jim Tressel, and I know the leader and person he is, and the things that happened that if that would happen now is is nothing. >> Right. It's crazy. >> wild. >> It's crazy. >> You know, the the the the world in which you coach and have to run a program based on At any rate, I just kind of wanted to bring that all up right here to to start our conversation. Uh which by the way, you're also entering your sixth season as Notre Dame head coach in five as a full-time um coach there. It's like time is flying for sure. The Rich Eisen Show is back on ESPN Radio along with Disney Plus and the ESPN app. Marcus Freeman, head coach of Notre Dame football, is here. Uh you know, I I met C.J. Carr for the first time as a little kid, you know, at a couple of Michigan events. Um he was probably like 6 years old, and I had a great chat with him the other day. He's just a really good kid with a lot of great stuff, um you know, inside and head on his shoulders. What's it like coaching him? >> Oh, man. You it's almost like you create a player, and what does that mean is that if you want a competitive football player that's a winner that is a leader that prepares like he does all those different things and he's he's gifted with ability but I think the thing that that you just mentioned is off the field. He's just the perfect individual and nobody's perfect but he is is such a great human being and it's a pleasure to coach him and be around him and to grow with him and and add on top of he's a heck of a quarterback and so he's making our team better and as I told him that's his greatest responsibility. It's not to throw touchdowns, win the Heisman, be a first round pick, it's to be the best leader he can be and make his teammates better cuz if he does that the rest of it will take care of himself. >> But that said, I mean the Heisman hype is already beginning. How do you handle that as a coach? >> I think my job is to continuously remind him of where his focus should be and that winning the Heisman is a reflection of a lot of different things and so he can either waste time focusing on winning the Heisman or he can continue to focus on the things that will make him the best football player he can be he does that but we all need reminders and and and that's my job is continuously remind him of what things are important. How do we take pressure off of you when you think about winning the Heisman and winning national championships those those that's high pressure. I mean the it's overwhelming but when you think about I got to have a good Monday and I got to be the best teammate I can be and I got to encourage guys, I got to hold them accountable and I got to prepare. Well, we can handle that and that's where his focus has to be continuously. >> I had my fun with him a little bit when we chatted coach because I asked him about how being left out of the college football playoffs last year affected him and how it's going to be potentially a chip on the shoulder of the team this year and he's like not really and then he revealed your motto for the year is leave no doubt. I'm like hold on a minute. Like that's not just coming out of the ether. So is that your message leave no doubt based on last year? It's the interpretation of the message. a lot of people are running with this thought of oh we have a chip on our shoulder. We have to leave no doubt this year because of what happened last year. No, I use it and we use it as a reminder to How do you leave no doubt today that this is the best Monday that you prepared tremendously? You did everything you were supposed to do to elevate on this Monday. And and that's how we're using it as a program is to leave no doubt with what we have guaranteed. And that's this game in front of us. That's the opportunity we have today and a chance to get better. And so if we do that over and over and over and over, then we'll leave no doubt for the season. But we're not focusing on that. We're using about leave no doubt today. Yeah, I know. But you're you're a whip smart individual. You're is you're not this is not your first rodeo. You know how it's going to be interpreted, right? Like leave no doubt. Like those moments that that that put an L on your sheet that cost you. Like leave no doubt cuz you could have you could have won right I I mean you you do see that part of it. Oh yeah, 100%. And and and here's here's how we also use it is that we left doubt last year. And it it's a our ability to not make an excuse and blame somebody else for not getting into the playoffs or not getting what we want. I think if every opportunity you you that that's a negative situation, you can either blame somebody else, but then you don't use it. How do you use it to get better? But if all of a sudden you say we left doubt. So it's our job to leave no doubt. Now you use it as an opportunity to evaluate everything you've done. We evaluate everything we did from January to fall. I mean through through August to say "How do we make sure that we're better prepared for week one? No matter who the opponent is. I don't care if it was Miami last year or Wisconsin this year. How do we ensure that we are at a higher elevation that doesn't determine the outcome of the game, right? That doesn't determine It's not determined by what the score of the game was. It was determined by Are we intentional about how we practice, how how much we practice, how much film? Are we a fresher team? All these different areas to make sure we're ready to go week one." >> Marcus Freeman here on the Rich Eisen Show. If you don't mind, I asked this of all your colleagues with the with your stature in the sport. You could wave a wand and make a rule to do something about getting more sense of what appears to have few rules that everybody follows together in the sport. What would it be? >> Oh, man. >> Yeah. What would it be? >> That is a a tough question to answer with just one with one thing. >> Okay. >> It really is. It's >> Well, if you want to go go if you want to expand it, go for it. >> You know, it's it's I think of a couple different things, right? I think of what's best for young people. the ability to transfer every year whenever they want or to the ability to transfer maybe one time or or whatever the we come up with, but I don't think it's it's best for young people to be able to transfer non-stop um without some type of of not punishment, but a you There's something that you you're something is taken away, which could be you have to sit out a year. and I say that because it when you you have to learn to overcome discomfort. You have to learn to overcome adversity. And it's not always a line to do that when at the end of the season if you don't love the situation you're at or maybe somebody's offering you more money, do you just get up and and and transfer every time? And so I am such an advocate for young people and I might not understood this at at 18 to 22, but I understand this now at my age and and that that we have to continue to find ways to help them learn to be self-sufficient and overcome some different challenges. >> And where do you stand on the fact that high school's no longer just the only feeder system into college, the National Football League as well. Where do you stand on that front? Coach. >> We I think I was asked that in the press conference the other day. We >> [snorts] >> you know, we we we can't number one admit a kid into school this late and think that they'll have a chance to succeed in the classroom and on the field. And so we our AD came out and and said he's in alignment with the Big Ten and the SEC with with not allowing guys that have signed professional contracts to come back to school. And so I'll let that speak for itself, but but at the same token like for me when they say the young man will not be prepared to have success if we admit him into school. We started school last week and they've gone through all their admissions process. Like that makes a lot of sense. We don't want to put these young people in jeopardy. >> Well, the thing I was talking about here too is what about all the kids that were busting their butts in spring and summer thinking that they have earned their spot, earned a certain number of snaps and then all of a sudden the Cleveland Browns cut somebody and you're going to you're going to have them come on the team two weeks before the season and say welcome, you know, come on like that's that ain't easy either. >> That's not easy and it's not right. And somebody could argue that, "Hey, okay, what if you get somebody hurt for the year?" Because you can't replace a guy that's out for the entire season. I just still don't don't I don't think that's great for college football to be able to do that. >> All right. A couple more minutes left with Marcus Freeman entering sixth season as Notre Dame head coach. Who is a worse helicopter dad, Jerome Bettis or Larry Fitzgerald? >> Neither of those two you don't ever see them around. >> They're not >> Uh you see them a game. You see them at the game. And and um they they support their their sons. It It's sometimes it's those ones that that maybe didn't play that uh they might be around more than than the Larry Fitzgeralds and the uh Jerome Bettises. >> Okay. So, they're they're not they're not helicoptering anywhere. >> No. >> No. Not making demands of uniform numbers or anything like that. We're not We're not seeing any of that. >> No. No. No. Now, like I'm not on I'm I'm not listening to the one-on-one conversations, >> right? I don't see my son's a wrestler at Cornell in his first year, and >> and I'm never there, but now we do have some some conversations um on the phone that maybe somebody said, "Man, you're a helicopter dad." Well, that's through the phone, you know? And so, >> Okay. All right. >> you know? But they're they're not here at practices, things like that. >> a bummer.
